id: Sir Mark Dunajtschik Mental Health Centre-67 Pilmuir Street, Epuni, Lower Hutt 5010, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Sir Mark Dunajtschik Mental Health Centre
venue: 67 Pilmuir Street, Epuni, Lower Hutt 5010, New Zealand
long_description:
The new Sir Mark Dunajtschik Mental Health Centre in Lower Hutt is a major investment in mental health infrastructure for the Wellington region. Construction commenced in June 2025 and this in-progress site visit is a rare opportunity to see a facility like this up close.

The purpose-built facility will provide 34 adult acute inpatient beds — 10 more than the existing facility — and is designed to support modern models of inpatient mental health care. The centre will provide safer, more therapeutic environments for people experiencing acute mental health distress, while giving clinical and support teams facilities better suited to delivering contemporary care.

The project is an important regional investment, aiming to improve patient and whānau outcomes, provide more appropriate care environments, and help reduce pressure on emergency departments.

NAWIC site visit focus: The project provides an opportunity to explore the delivery of a complex healthcare facility, with particular interest in construction, design, safety, services coordination and the creation of a therapeutic environment for patients, whānau and staff.

PPE: Full PPE required – Hard hat, safety vest, safety boots, long sleeves & pants

Accessibility: Note this project is in construction and flat access is not possible for this site visit.
Meeting Location: Meet at Site Gate, access is via 67 Pilmuir Street, next door to the old YMCA building.

Parking: Limited street parking is avilable in the areas.
Cost: Free for NAWIC Members. This is a Members only event – Not a NAWIC Member, Join today

Limited spots! Register now

Make sure you're following the NAWIC Wellington Humanitix page to stay in the loop and be the first to hear about upcoming events and announcements.

id: Understanding the Archive-129 Park Road, Miramar, Wellington 6022, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Understanding the Archive
venue: 129 Park Road, Miramar, Wellington 6022, New Zealand
long_description:
What happens to your film after delivery? Ngā Taonga has the answer.

Delivery isn't the end of your film's story. If the New Zealand Film Commission has funded your film, you're required to deposit it with Ngā Taonga Sound & Vision, Aotearoa's audiovisual archive. Most filmmakers tick that box and move on, but knowing how the archive works can make a real difference to your film's future.

Here's why:
Ngā Taonga preserves and catalogues your material, and when someone wants to screen it or access it, they send that request on to you as the rights holder. Nothing is released without your say. As the years go by, that becomes more and more valuable, whether it's a festival programmer, a researcher or a retrospective curator looking for your work.

So, who are they?
Ngā Taonga holds more than 800,000 audiovisual items dating back to 1894, and cares for the collections of the NZ Film Commission, Te Māngai Pāho, RNZ, TVNZ and much of NZ On Air's funded content, alongside material from Whakaata Māori, the Waitangi Tribunal and many other public and private collections. It's where our screen history lives, and where your work will sit alongside it.

As a filmmaker, it is essential that you know how to make sure your film materials are preserved and archived properly, so your work stays discoverable for generations to come.

Date: Wednesday 21st October
Time: Drinks from 6pm, event 6:30 - 8pm.
Location: Wētā Workshop Space, 129 Park Road, Miramar, Wellington.

Free for WIFT Members, $20 for non-members. Drinks & nibbles provided.

Our speakers:

Honiana Love (Te Ātiawa, Taranaki Iwi, Ngāruahine) Tumu Whakarae, Chief Executive of Ngā Taonga Sound & Vision.

Honiana has worked in archives and libraries for more than 25 years, including roles at Archives New Zealand, Te Reo o Taranaki and Manatū Taonga Ministry for Culture and Heritage. Honiana joined the Ngā Taonga leadership team in 2015 and has been Chief Executive since 2019. Her work has focused on strengthening relationships with iwi and communities, supporting appropriate access to taonga, and helping the Archive respond to the opportunities and challenges of digital preservation and access.

Louise McCrone, Pou Kohinga Taonga, General Manager Collection Management at Ngā Taonga Sound & Vision.

Louise has over 20 years-experience in archival practice and leadership ranging from specialist preservation work through leading teams responsible across conservation, repository management, collection development and digital preservation. Most recently she has played a role in the massive audiovisual Utaina digital preservation project and in the relocation of Archives New Zealand holdings to the new heritage campus.

Robin Laing, Moderator

Robin Laing is a film producer and founding Chair of WIFT.  She is currently working as a trustee and administrator for Aotearoa New Zealand Film Heritage Trust, established to ensure the back catalogue of New Zealand films is accessible for future audiences. 

Her industry work has included stints on the boards of Ngā Taonga, SPADA, NZFC, Copyright Council and the New Zealand International Film Festival where she is currently deputy Chair. As a film producer with a commitment to women’s stories and women filmmakers she has worked with directors Dame Gaylene Preston, Christine Jeffs, Niki Caro, Shirley Horrocks, Rebecca Tansley and Linda Niccol.

id: America After Trump: What will it mean for Asia and the World?-Hunter Building Kelburn Parade, Kelburn, Wellington 6012, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: America After Trump: What will it mean for Asia and the World?
venue: Hunter Building Kelburn Parade, Kelburn, Wellington 6012, New Zealand
long_description:
With the U.S. midterm elections just around the corner, the race to replace Donald Trump is just about to kick off. In this lecture, one of the sharpest observers of contemporary American foreign policy, Zack Cooper, will discuss how the American approach to foreign policy is changing and explore what a post-Trump world view might mean for Asia in particular.

Zack Cooper is a senior fellow at the American Enterprise Institute, where he studies US strategy in Asia, including alliance dynamics and US-China competition. He also teaches at Princeton University. He previously worked at the National Security Council and in the Office of the Secretary of Defense. Dr. Cooper is the author of Tides of Fortune: The Rise and Decline of Great Militaries from Yale University Press. He has also co-authored books, reports, and articles on US strategy and alliances in Asia. His writing has appeared in academic journals and popular press, including International Security, Security Studies, Foreign Affairs, the New York Times, the Washington Post, and the Wall Street Journal, among other outlets. Dr. Cooper graduated from Princeton University with a PhD and an MA in security studies and an MPA in international relations. He received a BA in public policy from Stanford University.

Refreshments will be provid at the event.

name: RIEDEL Wine Glass Experience in Wellington
venue: 3 Queens Wharf, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Did you know that the shape and size of your glass affects the aroma, flavour and overall profile of wine? Hosted by RIEDEL New Zealand's Managing Director, Mark Baulderstone, this interactive class reveals just how much the right glass can transform the way wine is experienced.

With four glasses from the refined and remarkably lightweight RIEDEL Veloce collection, you’ll discover firsthand why glass shape makes all the difference.

Drawing on decades of research into Grape Varietal Specific glassware, the hour-long session also offers insight into RIEDEL’s 270-year legacy of design and invention.

Your four glasses will be varietally matched with:

RIEDEL Veloce Sauvignon Blanc: Nautilus Sauvignon Blanc 2025

RIEDEL Veloce Chardonnay: Palliser Estate Chardonnay 2024

RIEDEL Veloce Pinot Noir: Misha's Vineyard Cantana Pinot Noir 2022

RIEDEL Veloce Shiraz: Yalumba Paradox Shiraz 2023

Tickets are strictly limited for this event - book now or miss out!

Every ticket includes a set of four RIEDEL Veloce glasses to take home, valued at $320:

This RIEDEL Wine Glass Experience is limited to adults 18+ only.

Please be aware there is no designated seating for this event. If you wish to be seated with a group, please arrive all together.

name: Restoring Sons & Daughters
venue: 22 Tennyson Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Restoring what was wounded. 

Recovering what was lost. 

Becoming who God created us to be.

 

Do you at times struggle to fully embrace your identity as a son or daughter of God? Do you feel like you know who you are in Christ, but struggle to walk in it completely?

Then this event is for you!

 

Join us for a powerful journey of healing, hope, restoration, and discovery of your identity in Christ led by Sandra Sellmer-Kersten.

Through biblical teaching, prayer ministry, and compassionate support, you’ll be invited to encounter Jesus in the places where you’ve experienced pain and discover His invitation to healing and wholeness.

Whether you are personally seeking healing or want to gain some tools to help others walk in and embrace their identity in Christ, this event offers practical insights, spiritual encouragement, and opportunities for prayer and ministry.

 

Sessions include:

The Heart: Restoring what has been wounded and broken.

The Identity: Remembering who God says we are—and learning to live from that truth.

The Voice: Recovering what shame, fear, pain, and rejection have silenced.

The Song: Reawakening the unique “song” God has sung over each of us from the beginning.

The Calling: Rediscovering what we were created for—and stepping into what God has entrusted to us with His power and authority. 

 

What to Expect:

Biblical teaching on trauma and healing

Opportunities to receive prayer

A safe, compassionate, and supportive environment

Encouragement, hope, and practical tools for restoration

Included in your ticket:

Morning and afternoon tea will be provided, but please bring your own lunch

A comprehensive manual, usually sold separately for $25

About Sandra:
Sandra Sellmer-Kersten is the founder of House of Nacham Ministries, New Zealand, which she leads alongside her husband, Peter. She previously served for nine years with Elijah House Ministries USA, where she worked as a prayer minister and teacher under the leadership of John and Paula Sandford. Since moving to New Zealand, Sandra began working alongside Elijah House New Zealand, where she facilitates schools, teaches lessons, and has served as a Small Group Leader for 14 years.

Sandra has a deep passion for seeing people encounter the healing love and transforming power of Jesus Christ. Through teaching, prayer ministry, mentoring, and training, she helps people understand the impact of trauma and woundedness, and to find healing, rediscover their God-given identity, and step more fully into who God created them to be.

Her teaching combines biblical truth, practical understanding, personal experience, and more than two decades of ministry experience, with an emphasis on creating a safe and compassionate space for people to honour their stories and encounter Jesus.

This event is not suitable for those under 16.

id: Hungary 1956–2026: 70 Years On - An evening of conversation, film and Hungarian hospitality-205 Ohiro Road, Brooklyn, Wellington 6021, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Hungary 1956–2026: 70 Years On - An evening of conversation, film and Hungarian hospitality
venue: 205 Ohiro Road, Brooklyn, Wellington 6021, New Zealand
long_description:
Hungary 1956–2026: 70 Years On

An evening of conversation, film and Hungarian hospitality

Join us at the Penthouse Cinema as we begin three days of events in Wellington commemorating the 70th anniversary of the 1956 Hungarian Revolution and Freedom Fight.

The evening opens with Hungarian nibbles and wine, followed by a panel discussion reflecting on the meaning and legacy of 1956 – revolution, freedom, resistance, displacement and the experience of starting again in a new country.

Panellists: Chris Finlayson, Alan Duff, Zoya Kőszegi and István Tóth
Moderator: Zsófia Hellyer

The discussion will be followed by a screening of the acclaimed Hungarian film Children of Glory (Szabadság, szerelem), set against the dramatic events of the 1956 Revolution and the Melbourne Olympic Games.

The film is in Hungarian with English subtitles.

Come for the whole evening or choose the parts of the programme you would like to attend.

Everyone is welcome – you don't need to be Hungarian or have any prior knowledge of the 1956 Revolution.

name: Jazz and Beyond Workshops 2026
venue: 91 Kelburn Parade, Kelburn, Wellington 6012, New Zealand  ·  Accessibility info
long_description:
Jazz and Beyond for students 19 and under

December 14–17, 2026

Coordinated by Chris Beernink, Dave Wilson, Daniel Hayles, Andrew Faleatua, Lance Philip. Proudly supported by the Tauranga Jazz Society.

Take it to the next level as a player or vocalist at the Jazz and Beyond Workshops! Young musicians from across Aotearoa come together to dive into jazz and connected styles, working closely with some of the country’s leading performers and educators. In a friendly, inclusive environment, you’ll grow your skills, make new musical connections, and learn alongside other students your age from all around the motu.

Here’s what’s in store:

small group ensembles led by professional musicians

developing improvisation skills in supportive settings

an introduction to music production

listening sessions that expand your skills

inclusive jam sessions where all are welcome

ensemble performances at the end of week concert

And more!

If you're 19 or under with at least a year of experience on your instrument or in vocal training, you’re welcome to join. Choose from trumpet, trombone, saxophone, clarinet, flute, bass, piano, guitar, drums, vibraphone, or voice.

The workshops are held at the New Zealand School of Music–Te Kōkī at Te Herenga Waka-Victoria University of Wellington. Follow the Jazz and Beyond Workshops on Instagram or Facebook for the latest updates. Email jazzandbeyondworkshops@gmail.com with any questions.

Schedule

The workshops run 9:00am-4:30pm Monday through Thursday, with evening activities including concerts and our inclusive jam sessions Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday. Students perform in a closing concert on Thursday afternoon.

Accommodation

Students arrange their own accommodation. Often students from outside Wellington stay together in groups with a parent chaperone. Options for housing near Victoria University of Wellington include backpacker hostels and hotels. If you have a group of 15 or more, University Student Housing may be an option. Email jazzandbeyondworkshops@gmail.com if you'd like to pursue this option.

Meals

Lunch for the four days is available for purchase at many convenient locations on campus, or students may bring their own lunch.

Equipment

Provided equipment includes drum kits, guitar and bass amps, pianos/keyboards, microphones and PAs for vocalists.

All brass and wind players should bring their own instruments.

Drummers: you are required to bring your own cymbals, sticks, and hi-hat clutch.

Guitarists and bass players: you are required to bring your own instruments as well as cables (leads).

Preparation

All students with one year of experience on an instrument or in vocal training have the skills required to participate, so no musical preparation is required. On the first day, students will play a very short audition to be placed in an appropriate ensemble. Guidelines for this short audition will be sent to all registered participants in advance of the workshops.

Cost

Early bird price: $325 - register before 19th October

Standard price $350 - on or after 19th October

Registration is open to all until all spots are filled.

We are dedicated to ensuring all students can participate in the workshops without financial constraints. If the cost poses a barrier, please email us at jazzandbeyondworkshops@gmail.com and we will find a solution to facilitate your participation!

long_description:
NYMPHO welcomes Chippy Nonstop to Pōneke in collaboration with her own party series, PEP RALLY, for a cross-continental meeting on the dancefloor. One for the history books.

Chippy Nonstop is a versatile DJ, rapper, and producer whose high-energy sets seamlessly blend global club, rap, and bass-driven sounds. She thrives across contexts from queer-focused underground nights to fashion events and more commercial stages bringing her unique energy to every floor. Key shows include Berghain, Live From Earth, DGTL, Ultra, the Mugler Fashion Show and has shared lineups with VTSS, LSDXOXO, Honey Dijon and many more. Chippy also runs her own party series and upcoming label Pep Rally, centering FLINTA, BIPOC, and queer representation*.

LINEUP:

CHIPPY NONSTOP (CAN)

BABETECH

CURRENT BIAS

WELMIE

ODEIOUS

DOOM100001B2B75ARROWHEADS

MC MAN(K)ILA

NYMPHO is a dance-focused queer club night with visual and performance art styles woven into high energy DJ sets. We strive to create a safe, inclusive and transcendent club experience which celebrates gender euphoria, body positivity and sexual liberation. Our kaupapa of lifting up marginalised communities extends from our audience and lineups to our musical philosophies - with genre-diverse sets centred around QBIPOC rooted genres such as techno, house and emergent queer sounds. As well as spotlighting the best of Aotearoa’s diverse queer talent, NYMPHO has brought international icons to our long white cloud, including Isabella Lovestory, horsegiirL, Doss, TAAHLIAH, Ninajirachi, Umru, MGNA Crrrta, Kevin Aviance, MikeQ, Pxssy Palace, Jasmine Infiniti, Estoc, Clearcast and DJ G2G.

Ki ngā iwi Mana Whenua ō Te Whanganui-a-Tara, tēnei te tuku mihi ki ā koutou katoa. We acknowledge Te Āti Awa, Ngāti Mutunga, Ngāti Tama, Ngāti Ruanui, Taranaki Whānui, Ngāti Toa Rangatira as Mana Whenua of Wellington/Te Whanganui-a-Tara.

May the flames of your peoples never extinguish, but only to burn brighter. Thank you for your enduring presence! Mauri Ora!! 🖤🤍❤️

Concession tickets are available for low wage, unemployed or financially insecure nymphs. If you can't afford a ticket you can get in touch with us via Instagram. No nymphs left behind!

EPILEPSY WARNING: Strobe lighting and other intense lighting effects will be used during this show. It will not be safe for those with epilepsy and other conditions with sensitivity to light.

long_description:
‘TONES of SILENCE’ – FUTUNA CHAPEL in BLACK & WHITE - PUBLIC TALKS 2026

The ‘Tones of Silence’ exhibition explores through B & W photography taken with vintage camera and lenses to give another way of viewing and experiencing the Chapel. This exhibition will reveal the tones, textures, composition and forms of the Chapel in black and white with many shades of grey.

Step inside Futuna Chapel for three captivating Sunday afternoon talks covering black-and-white photography, heritage architecture, and Aotearoa New Zealand’s built history, from 2:00pm to 3:30pm during the Futuna Exhibition.

The Trust looks forward to welcoming architects, designers, graduates, students and interested members of the public to attend these events and support the Trust in its work.

The Futuna Trust is a charitable organisation and all koha received from the WHF events will go towards the ongoing care, maintenance and operation of Futuna Chapel and also to support various initiatives undertaken by the Trust. 

Please register to attend the public talks to ensure you get a seat. Seats are limited. There is no set ticket price. The gift of koha is prefered.

name: Secrets of Successful Cross-Sectoral Collaborations Seen Through the Project Management Lens
venue: 139 Vivian Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Note: This is an in-person only event at Victoria University of Wellington 139 Vivian Street, Te Aro Campus

About this event:

Many challenges faced by modern society require extensive partnerships and collaboration of organisations, teams and individuals from multiple disciplines and sectors. Building skills for working across sectors is not a luxury – it is a necessity.

In this talk, Dr Sandra Mandic will introduce a framework for planning and managing cross-sector collaborations outlined in her recently published book “Compass Guide: Secrets of Successful Cross-Sector Collaborations”. She will focus on discussing project and programme management aspects of the framework, sharing her insights from initiating and leading the BEATS Research Programme in 2013-2023 – a world-class example of a successful cross-sector collaboration.

Attendees will have opportunity to reflect on their own experiences with cross-sectoral work and share their insights.

About the Presenter:

Dr Sandra Mandic, PhD, PMP is a transformational leader, innovator and award-winning researcher and author. Sandra’s personal and professional journey spans nine cities across five countries and three continents – including Europe, Canada, United States and New Zealand. She speaks four languages and has experience of working in academia, government and business. Sandra is the founder and the director of the research consultancy AGILE Research Ltd. and the creator of the Compass Guide Research Training resources (six Compass Guide books and over dozen courses) which link research and project management. She is recipient of the New Zealand Academic Achievement in Project Management Award (finalist in 2024 and winner in 2025) from PMINZ for two of her books.

Sandra is also a Research Associate at Auckland University of Technology, Team Leader Transport Strategy at Wellington City Council and was the founder and principal investigator on the award-winning BEATS Research Programme (2013-2023).

What rituals are and why they are important

Why rituals matter in workplaces

The difference between habits and rituals

In depth knowledge of each of the 4 parts of the deck and why they are important

How to use our PARR model to craft rituals that stick

How to guide groups through ideation, crafting and action

id: The Trajectory of the Indian Economy over the Past Four Decades: A Story of Mixed Experiences-16 Kelburn Parade, Kelburn, Wellington 6012, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: The Trajectory of the Indian Economy over the Past Four Decades: A Story of Mixed Experiences
venue: 16 Kelburn Parade, Kelburn, Wellington 6012, New Zealand
long_description: The lecture will discuss India’s developmental experience over the past four decades. Since this is a vast subject, the discussion will be limited to only some of the principal features. India’s experience is one of mixed messages, both positive and negative. India historically recorded a low growth rate, around 3.5%. This was accompanied by a high tariff regime along with bureaucratic controls that have been described as a ‘license permit raj’. India experienced a serious balance of payments crisis in 1991 with foreign reserves barely enough to pay for 2 weeks’ food imports. This set in motion a series of trade liberalisation reforms initiated by the then Finance Minister, Dr Manmohan Singh, consisting of removal of trade barriers and reduction of high tariffs on several items. This propelled India to one of the fastest growing economies accompanied by increase in per capita income and reduction in poverty. India ranks third on aggregate GDP (on PPP) though on per capita GDP she falls well down the list. India’s sizeable middle-class swamps that of the EU and many of the smaller economies thus providing a large market. There has been widespread digitalisation of transactions leading to reduction in corruption. But there has also been a large increase in inequality and according to the World Inequality report, 2026, India is one of the most unequal countries in the world. There is lack of skilled jobs to employ the educated youth making India unable to exploit the advantage of ‘demographic dividend’ she enjoys over China. The talk will compare living standards between India and China.

venue: 6 Myrtle Street, Hutt Central, Lower Hutt 5040, New Zealand
long_description:
Power Up the Hutt – Central Lower Hutt

A more comfortable home. Lower energy bills. Greater peace of mind.

If you've been wondering whether electrification could make a real difference to your home and your household budget, this free community event is the perfect place to start.

Join us at Hutt Bowling Club, 6 bMyrtle Street on Thursday 29 October at 7:30 pm for an informative and welcoming evening where local people share how they've transformed the way they live.

From warmer homes in winter and lower running costs to cleaner indoor air and greater energy independence, electrification is helping Hutt Valley households enjoy a better quality of life while reducing their environmental impact.

You'll hear firsthand experiences from local residents who have installed heat pumps, solar panels, home batteries, electric hot water systems, induction cooktops and electric vehicles. They'll explain what motivated them, what the process was like, what they would do differently, and the benefits they're now enjoying every day.

Whether you're just beginning to explore your options or you're ready to take the next step, you'll leave with practical ideas, greater confidence, and a clearer understanding of where to begin.

This is a community event—not a sales presentation. There are no technical lectures or pressure to buy anything. Just honest conversations, practical advice, and the opportunity to ask questions in a relaxed and friendly setting.

Businesses, schools and community organisations interested in electrification are also welcome.

Free admission. Everyone welcome.

Come along and discover how simple changes today can create a home that's more comfortable, more affordable to run, and better prepared for the future.

long_description:
04butchclub presents SAPPHIC SESSION - a night showcasing some local sapphic and FLINTA* talent of Te Whanganui-a-Tara.

Why We're Here

Live music hits differently when you're surrounded by your community so it's about time this happens for Te Whanganui-a-Tara sapphic/FLINTA* scene. In this dedicated FLINTA* space, you will be serenaded by incredibly talented musicians and artists based in Te Whanganui-a-Tara.

As a bonus reason to party, this space was created to honour International Lesbian Day - a global celebration with deep local roots believed to have kicked off right here in Te Whanganui-a-Tara back in the 1980s!

Introducing: The Mad Butches (2026 'Make a Band' Project)

To shake things up and get talent back on stage, 04butchclub launched a 'make a band' project. In true community spirit, we gathered a group of keen singers and musicians - who haven't performed in a hot minute and had never met each other before - straight into a practice room. They've decided to be known as The Mad Butches, and maybe there's a good reason for it? Come witness the raw, collaborative magic of their very first live set!

What to expect on the night:

Open mic karaoke in the first 30min, or grab the guitar and sing a song as everyone filters in and settles into the scene.

An epic lineup - please see below for artists involved.

A couple of pool tables.

A chill, seated area for when you need to take a breather.

A table where you can enrol to vote, if you haven't already.

Timeline:

7.00pm - Doors open and open mic - choose your poison: karaoke or with guitar

7.30pm - Slam poetry from Lo

7.50pm - Comet

8.20pm - Danica Bryant

9.05pm - Mad Butches

10.05pm - Gift Horse

11.00pm - Event finish

Accessibility inside the venue:

Single-level access throughout the main venue except for the VIP area, which is up a flight of stairs.

Flashing lights (from stage and photographers) and loud sounds will be present.

Free foam earplugs will be available all night.

name: Mum Club - Mum's & Bub's October
venue: 35 Oxford Street, Tawa, Wellington 5028, New Zealand  ·  Accessibility info
long_description:
Mum's & Bub's — A 4-Week Connection Series

Join us for a relaxed, expert-led series designed to support you through those early postpartum months - no pressure, no judgement, just a space to connect.

Each week we welcome a different guest expert to share their knowledge and answer your questions on the topics that matter most after having a baby. While you listen, chat and ask away, bub has their own comfy little play space set up right there in the room - so there's no need to juggle or step away.

Sessions are split by age group, so you're with mums at a similar stage

Each day there are three session time options - 10.15am, 11.30am

🚼 Thursdays
Starting Thursday 8th October, running for 4 weeks

Week 1 — Thursday 8th October: Lactation/Feeding/Pumping with Jo from BlissfulBubs

Week 2 — Thursday 15th October: Starting Solids with Dr Julie from Dr Julie Bhosale

Week 3 — Thursday 22nd October: Naturopathic postpartum care with Anna from Anna Reeves Naturopathy

Week 4 — Thursday 29th October: Sleep with Fran from thegentlesleepconsultant

Each session is limited to 10 mums to keep the space calm and supportive. When selecting the ticket - this will be the time group you're in each week, and the ticket price covers all 4 weeks.

What's Included

A new guest expert each week, covering key postpartum topics

Open Q&A - bring your questions, nothing is off-limits

A comfy, safe play space for bub within the session

Light morning tea provided

Time to connect with other local mums going through the same stage

☕ BYO coffee welcome (with lid to keep babies safe)

Pricing

$120 for the full 4 weeks (Girl maths $30 per session)

Pricing is per Mum - so twin/multiple mums only need the 1 ticket

What to Know

Feeding, crying and leaving early are all completely okay

We'll come together as a group at the start to introduce ourselves - no pressure to be on time, the doors will stay open, and the expert talk is expected to begin around 20 minutes in

These sessions are suited for first-time or multiple-time mums. Tickets are per mum (twin mums just need the one ticket)

For the women who have started their investment journey, dabbled in a few areas and feel pretty confident about how markets work, and are now ready for the next step - with a little support.

This workshop is your opportunity to get in a room with a Financial Adviser and review your portfolio in real time.

Elizabeth is highly qualified and experienced, but maybe more importantly, she is relatable.

As a chronic over-thinker, only child and high achiever she knows how easy it is to move too fast and commit to a range of solutions (e.g. investments) and after the fact second-guess whether they were the correct options!

If you have more than 2 investments, whether they are KiwiSaver, another Super scheme, Sharesies, Property, Term Deposits, Index Funds or Managed Funds (yes there is a difference!) then there is a good chance you are no longer able to see what your overall portfolio looks like, the risk level you are taking across the board, and whether these investments are actually getting you to where you want to be.

This workshop is limited to a very small number of women because we will be:

Discussing risk profile and money personality

Bringing in some Financial Planning concepts

Looking at some more complex concepts around building a portfolio

Looking at your personal portfolio in detail and how it aligns (or not!) with where you want to be

This workshop is ideal for anyone who has started their investing journey with enthusiasm and confidence but is now realising they've got a range of investments to manage and need clarity on how to move forward. Investments should be a tool to get to the financial future you want, let's make sure they are doing their job!

You bring your investment info, I'll bring the expertise and with some lovely women and delicious refreshments we will take a hard look at whether you are on track for where you want to go!

There will be some pre and post workshop comms and questions to ensure you get maximum value from this event.

The advantage of having an actual adviser run this event? For those that are genuinely ready to start building wealth after the workshop, there is the opportunity to work with Elizabeth 1:1 and put together a personalised Financial Plan.

Check out www.yourworth.co.nz for more details about Elizabeth and Know Your Worth.

long_description:
Led by 9-year-old (yes, 9 years old!) drumming phenom TomTom Woodson, TomTom and the Groove-Daddies play a sing-out-loud style of music that includes hits from the Beatles, CCR, the Killers, the Rolling Stones and more.

From an early age, TomTom showed an aptitude for music such that around the age of 10 months, his father bought him a set of drumsticks and made him a small drum kit out of milk formula cans. TomTom immediately began playing along to his father’s guitar playing and before he was 2 years old, TomTom performed his first gig in public. His father contacted his professional musician friends and in 2022, The Groove-Daddies were formed. The band features Jay Hay on bass guitar and TomTom’s father Beau Redding on guitar and lead vocals. In 2026 they performed at the Festival of Lights in New Plymouth and at the Picton Maritime Festival.

We've designed a Christmas experience for the whole family!

As a family, come along and enter our amazing, indoor, interactive Christmas festival! The theme is Joy to the World - come along and experience the joy of Christmas traditions and experiences from around the globe!

Enjoy hands-on crafts and activities from around the world together, get into some fun games at your own pace, singalong to live music and hear a Christmas story, take a break in the quiet space with relevant activities, tuck into our delish loaded free hot chocolates and cookie bar, get your annual whanau photo in our dress up photobooth, take time to remember someone special at the remembrance tree... and many more merry and marvellous festivities!

Joy to the World: A Christmas Experience is all about getting into the Christmas spirit - our hope is that we can support families in the Miramar community through this event!

Tickets are $3 per child or adult / $13 for a group of 5.
Please note: if you require more than 5 tickets, please add any additional individual or group tickets to make up your group total.

There are no additional costs on the day - all activities and food onsite is part of the ticket fee.

All proceeds from this event will go towards providing Christmas gifts and support for families in the Miramar community. Thank you for your support!

Simply book tickets for your prefered session using this website! Please reserve tickets for any adults AND kids attending.





SESSION TIMES:

There are three Joy to the World sessions over the weekend. Each session is up to 90mins.

Saturday 28 November: 9.30 - 11am

Saturday 28 November: 11am - 12.30pm

Saturday 28 November: 1.30pm - 3pm

Please note: All children under the age of 13 must be accompanied by an adult.

name: Awakening the Subtle Body with Joan Hyman
venue: Level 1/175 Vivian Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
About the training

This immersive training invites you to awaken the subtle body through the practice of yoga. The subtle body is the energetic field that connects body, breath and mind.

Over the course of this 3-day training, we explore how movement, breath and awareness shape the flow of prana. Through asana, pranayama and meditation, you will deepen your connection to the more subtle layers of your practice and refine how you move, breathe and sequence with intention.

What you will explore

The foundations of yoga energetics including prana, nadis, bandhas and chakras

the relationship between physical alignment and the energetic flow

Sequencing as a tool to guide prana through the body

Pranayama and meditation as gateways to the subtle body

Safe and intelligent progressions toward more advanced postures

Any questions? Head to our FAQ at the bottom of the page.

SCHEDULE

The training is 3 full days with each day designed to lead on to the next. Lunch break is from 12-1:30pm.

Friday 9am - 4pm - Sequencing towards arm balances

We explore sequencing as a roadmap for practice and learn how arm balances support lightness, strength and flow. Themes include prana, the five koshas, bandhas and biomechanics as a gateway to the subtle body. The day ends with pranayama practice.

Saturday 9am - 4pm - Sequencing towards inversions and inner body awareness

A deeper exploration of inversions and their effect on the inner body. We study the nadis and sushumna and how sequencing supports inward awareness. The day closes with restorative postures and meditation.

Sunday 9am - 3:30pm - Sequencing for backbends and subtle body integration

Backbends to uplift prana and access the more subtle layers of practice. We will explore the chakras as the most refined energetic layer and integrate everything through sequencing, meditation, and pranayama. A quiet inward ending to conclude the training.

THE VENUE: BHAKTI LOUNGE

The Bhakti Lounge is located in the heart of Wellington CBD, at level 1, 175 Vivian Street. It has been operating for twenty plus years and is 100% volunteer-run, community first events space.

YOUR TEACHER

Joan Hyman, Senior Yoga Teacher and founder of the School of Yoga (USA)

Joan Hyman is the director and founder of The School of Yoga, an authentic international teacher training program focused on continuing education. Her grounded teaching style seamlessly supports her students as they emerge from their practice with the rich and bright energy that yoga has to offer.

Joan’s teachings come from an organic and intuitive place, as she draws upon the combined studies of Ashtanga and Iyengar yoga as well as Ayurveda and meditation. An authentic modern-day yogi, Joan's love and devotion show up in her practice and throughout her teaching. You will leave her class feeling transformed and deeply aligned.

Joan spent fifteen years as a distinguished YogaWorks Senior Teacher before bringing her expertise to Wanderlust as the Director of Teacher Trainings in 2016. Now, with over twenty years of experience leading retreats, trainings, and international workshops, Joan travels the globe and teaches online, leading her own signature trainings. She has created The School of Yoga, which is a professional education program, helping students and inspiring teachers to work towards their five hundred hours Yoga Alliance Certification. A leader in the yoga community, Joan’s open-hearted approach to teaching yoga keeps both her inner spirit and her students continuously evolving.

YOUR HOSTS

Sarah Marriott and Liz Birkett

Yoga teachers (500YTT) Sarah Marriott and Liz Birkett warmly welcome you! Having studied with Joan Hyman since 2018, they are excited to bring her to Wellington shores once again, so she can share her extensive knowledge of Yoga with Aotearoa's Yoga community. 

FAQ

How much is the 3 day training?

It is $520 (early bird) however this increases to $550 from November 1st, 2026.

Can I attend one or two days?

Sorry, no. This is a 3 day training with each day designed to lead on to the next. Please email Sarah and Liz if you have further questions about this.

Who is this training for?

This training is for dedicated practitioners and teachers who feel curious about the energetics behind the physical practice and who want to deepen their experience beyond alignment alone. This training is open to teachers and dedicated yoga practitioners. You do not need to be a teacher to join. A regular yoga practice and curiosity to dive deeper is enough!

Do I need to bring a yoga mat or any props?

We have mats, and props (blocks, straps bolsters) however you are welcome to bring your own.

Is there parking at the venue?

Street parking:
Best option is to Uber or car pool if you can as street parking is capped at 2 hours (around $5 per hour) during the week and 3 hours (around $3/4) in the weekend.

Car parks:
The Hope Gibbons Parking (68 Taranaki Street) is a 2-3 minute walk from the venue or there are other parking buildings 5 minutes away (E.g., Garrett Street Car Park)

What are the lunch options?

Of course you are welcome to bring your own lunch/snacks. However, there are plenty of cafes and restaurants available to you on nearby Cuba street. You have 1.5 hours for lunch so you may like to dine in, take a drive or head to Oriental Pde for a walk!

The Bhakti lounge also serves a delicious plant-based lunch Mon-Fri at a very affordable price.

I'm from out of town. Is there accommodation nearby?

Yes there are plenty of options just a short walk away.

id: Understanding the Archive-129 Park Road, Miramar, Wellington 6022, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Understanding the Archive
venue: 129 Park Road, Miramar, Wellington 6022, New Zealand
long_description:
What happens to your film after delivery? Ngā Taonga has the answer.

Delivery isn't the end of your film's story. If the New Zealand Film Commission has funded your film, you're required to deposit it with Ngā Taonga Sound & Vision, Aotearoa's audiovisual archive. Most filmmakers tick that box and move on, but knowing how the archive works can make a real difference to your film's future.

Here's why:
Ngā Taonga preserves and catalogues your material, and when someone wants to screen it or access it, they send that request on to you as the rights holder. Nothing is released without your say. As the years go by, that becomes more and more valuable, whether it's a festival programmer, a researcher or a retrospective curator looking for your work.

So, who are they?
Ngā Taonga holds more than 800,000 audiovisual items dating back to 1894, and cares for the collections of the NZ Film Commission, Te Māngai Pāho, RNZ, TVNZ and much of NZ On Air's funded content, alongside material from Whakaata Māori, the Waitangi Tribunal and many other public and private collections. It's where our screen history lives, and where your work will sit alongside it.

As a filmmaker, it is essential that you know how to make sure your film materials are preserved and archived properly, so your work stays discoverable for generations to come.

Date: Wednesday 21st October
Time: Drinks from 6pm, event 6:30 - 8pm.
Location: Wētā Workshop Space, 129 Park Road, Miramar, Wellington.

Free for WIFT Members, $20 for non-members. Drinks & nibbles provided.

Our speakers:

Honiana Love (Te Ātiawa, Taranaki Iwi, Ngāruahine) Tumu Whakarae, Chief Executive of Ngā Taonga Sound & Vision.

Honiana has worked in archives and libraries for more than 25 years, including roles at Archives New Zealand, Te Reo o Taranaki and Manatū Taonga Ministry for Culture and Heritage. Honiana joined the Ngā Taonga leadership team in 2015 and has been Chief Executive since 2019. Her work has focused on strengthening relationships with iwi and communities, supporting appropriate access to taonga, and helping the Archive respond to the opportunities and challenges of digital preservation and access.

Louise McCrone, Pou Kohinga Taonga, General Manager Collection Management at Ngā Taonga Sound & Vision.

Louise has over 20 years-experience in archival practice and leadership ranging from specialist preservation work through leading teams responsible across conservation, repository management, collection development and digital preservation. Most recently she has played a role in the massive audiovisual Utaina digital preservation project and in the relocation of Archives New Zealand holdings to the new heritage campus.

Robin Laing, Moderator

Robin Laing is a film producer and founding Chair of WIFT.  She is currently working as a trustee and administrator for Aotearoa New Zealand Film Heritage Trust, established to ensure the back catalogue of New Zealand films is accessible for future audiences. 

Her industry work has included stints on the boards of Ngā Taonga, SPADA, NZFC, Copyright Council and the New Zealand International Film Festival where she is currently deputy Chair. As a film producer with a commitment to women’s stories and women filmmakers she has worked with directors Dame Gaylene Preston, Christine Jeffs, Niki Caro, Shirley Horrocks, Rebecca Tansley and Linda Niccol.

It's gonna be a big session filled with emotional highs and lows and filled to the coffee cup brim with lore. So if you're a Twin Peaks fan you can't miss this one!

long_description:
CLUEDUNNIT

DINNER WITH 'MURDER ON THE MENU'

Step into a world of intrigue, suspense, and unforgettable entertainment as InterContinental Wellington partners with Cluedunnit to present an immersive murder mystery dining experience. Guests will be transported into a captivating story where secrets unfold, clues emerge, and every guest becomes part of the investigation.

Combining exceptional hospitality with live theatrical entertainment, Cluedunnit invites guests to enjoy a delicious dining experience while questioning suspects, following leads, and working together to solve a thrilling mystery. From the moment you arrive, you'll be immersed in a world of drama, laughter, and unexpected twists.

Whether you're planning a unique night out with friends, celebrating a special occasion, or enjoying an unforgettable evening with colleagues, Cluedunnit at InterContinental Wellington promises the perfect blend of fine dining, mystery, and entertainment.

Guests will interact with a live cast of characters, uncover clues, and work together to crack the case, all while enjoying a delicious three-course dinner.

But beware, all is not as it seems. As secrets unravel and tensions rise, you'll need to decipher the clues, question the suspects, and piece together the evidence before it's too late. After all, where there's a will, there's a murder.

Where there's a mystery, there's a motive. Where there's a motive, there's a murder. The question is: whodunnit?

MURDER AT THE MANOR - The Story So Far...

It is 1929 and this English Cotswold beauty spot is celebrating the life of elderly heiress Rose Stimper, who, in an act of philanthropy, has bequeathed the village a large sum of money and left instructions that the villagers must decide how best to spend it. 

This will be a party like no other. Everyone has ideas on how to spend the money, and the entire village turns out to attend Pokeingham Hall, which has been thrown open for the first time in many years to host the event.

But beware, all is not as it seems. There are dark forces at work.

Enjoy a delicious three course dinner as you question the suspects, decipher the clues and work to crack the case. And please remember - where there’s a will, there’s a murder!

Dark blood chocolate mousse, with raspberry and dark chocolate crumble.

1 or 2 Day Presentation Skills Workshop

When effective presenters speak, they do more than inform - they influence, persuade, and inspire. That isn’t down to magic or your personality; it’s method. With the right tools, anyone can build genuine connection and move a room.

This workshop is for leaders, emerging leaders, technical specialists, and professionals who want practical tools and techniques for speaking in both formal and informal settings.

Short on time? Attend 1 Day (Foundations) for all the core skills. Ready for a bigger shift? Choose 2 Days (Advanced) for one on one coaching and deeper transformation. Pick what’s right for you.

The workshop format

Small group format for maximum practice and feedback (no massive groups).

Plan engaging content (fast)

Plan faster, make better decisions about what to include (and what to ditch).

 

Design useful slides (not wallpaper)

A simple but revolutionary way to design slides that support - not sabotage - your message.

Practical guidance on using AI to fast-track draft slides and create supporting documents (and how to avoid creating AI slop!)

How to use PowerPoint to keep you on track without putting your audience to sleep.

 

Keep nerves under control

A proven psychological approach to calm the mental chatter that causes waffling, speed talking, and blank moments.

Build a personal plan to shift focus from “me” to the audience and the outcome you want.

 

Deliver in a natural, engaging way

Three delivery techniques that help you look credible, be engaging and feel confident.

(For more intensive delivery coaching, check out Day Two)

 

Plenty of practice

You’ll practise each technique in pairs or threes - supportive, safe, and highly practical.

Over two full days, you’ll create a significant shift in your communication skills.

Day One gives you the foundations to make presenting easier and more effective.

Day Two consolidates and extends these skills. You’ll go deeper into content planning, adapt the tools to your real work presentations, and get personalised coaching to develop your own authentic style.

You’ll also learn strategies for handling even the toughest audiences. The workshop is practical, hands-on, and focused on learning by doing - presenting, receiving coaching, and observing your peers.

If you’re ready for lasting, transformative change in your communication skills, the two-day option is the best choice.

What you’ll learn

Everything from Day 1 (Foundations) PLUS

Go deeper with planning

Apply the SpeakerMap to plan an actual presentation that you can give. 

Dive deeper into crafting valuable messages that you can use in the future. 

Rehearse in a way that actually works

A practical way to prepare when time is tight — so you own your words.

Shift from competent to compelling

One-on-one coaching targeted to your specific needs.

Video feedback plus our inside-out coaching methodology to reconnect you with the techniques you use naturally in conversation.

How to use silence, pace, notes, and the remote without looking stiff or artificial.

How to speak with energy and authenticity, not speed and panic.

Eliminate “ums” and “ahs”, look confident (even when you’re not), and create a sense of commitment that audiences feel.

An understanding of your personal communication strengths and the areas you need to focus on for growth.


Handle audiences like a pro

Strategies for side chats, interruptions, distractions, disagreement, and the odd angry voice - while staying calm and in control.

To help teachers, parents, whānau, and communities make informed choices in the 2026 General Election, PPTA Te Wehengarua Wellington Region is hosting an election forum. Doors will open at 5.45pm, with welcomes and introductions at 6pm. The formal part of the evening will finish at 7.30pm with light refreshments being served.

Anyone is welcome to attend, but you must register through Humanitix. This event is run by volunteers and members of the Post-Primary Teachers Association Wellington Region. PPTA is the professional association and union of secondary teachers and principals in Aotearoa New Zealand.

long_description:
🎵 Beautiful Chamber Music with a Magical View🎵 Comfy Concert🎻 Saturday 24 October, 4 - 6PM

Relax with a cuppa and enjoy exquisite live music from The Chamber Pot Pourri Ensemble & special guests!

The Comfy Concert on 24 October features Anna Gawn, mezzo soprano (formerly of the Kugels klezmer band), Anna van der Zee (violin), Nick Hancox (viola), Ross Harris (accordion), alongside Helene Pohl (violin) and Rolf Gjelsten (cello).This is a very special event  - a launch of new CD Moriamur and with performances by top classical musicians. The afternoon is headlined by a klezmer-inspired song-cycle for mezzo soprano and string quartet by Harris, along with a vivacious violin-cello duo by Erwin Schulhoff.

Two pieces composed by Ross Harris will be performed at the Comfy Concert in Roseneath on Saturday 24th. Harris, Arts Laureate and one of New Zealand's most revered and versatile composers, wrote both pieces specially for Anna Gawn, who will perform for us this afternoon! The first, is a world premiere of Moriamur for mezzo soprano and string quartet - a song cycle based on the story of doomed love of Dido and Aeneas, with words taken from the 4th Book of Virgil's The Aeneid. The second work (Songs for Dark Times) is a series of songs for mezzo soprano, string quartet and accordion, originally written for the klezmer group The Kugels.

Tickets:

$45 General Admission

$10 Students with ID

$5 Children under 15yo

Doors open from 3:30pm

Please join us early for light refreshment and to get comfy before the performance starts at 4.

Or you may like to bring a picnic with friends to sit outside from 3o'clock and enjoy the amazing view,

Connect in person with Aotearoa New Zealand’s EdTech community.

Hosted by EdTechNZ Member  Alsu Sworder from Litmaps, this is an informal event that could formally change the trajectory of your life.

Come along to meet others building, supporting and scaling education technology. Whether you’re an EdTech founder, educator, investor, industry partner or simply interested in the future of learning, this is an opportunity to connect with the community.

Light finger food and drinks provided courtesy of our friends at Litmaps. 

Registration

EdTechNZ members and non-members are welcome. Please register so we can plan for numbers.

Not in Wellington?

If you want to arrange your own regular local EdTech connect events, let us know and we can help you set this up — email us at info@edtechnz.org.nz. EdTechNZ currently hosts year-round in-person Connect events in Auckland, Wellington, Hamilton, Christchurch and Dunedin.

About our event partner Litmaps
Litmaps is a literature review and research discovery tool that helps researchers, students and professionals find relevant academic papers faster, understand how research connects, and stay up to date with new publications. Using citation networks and visual maps, Litmaps makes it easier to discover important research, identify gaps and organise literature. Used by researchers in more than 150 countries, Litmaps is proud to be an EdTechNZ member and supporter of the New Zealand EdTech community.

“A mix of huskiness and honey, Peregian singer, songwriter and acoustic guitarist Mark Moroney’s voice acts like a balm.” Frances Frangenheim, Salt Magazine.

Singer song writer and guitarist Mark Moroney radiates emotion, authenticity and soul.  His style and sound are distilled from a musical melting pot of folk, blues, roots, soul, jazz and pop. 

A favourite at festivals including Woodford Folk Festival (AU), The Mosaic Music Festival (Singapore), & The Bay Of Islands Jazz & Blues Festival (NZ), experiencing Mark live is an unmissable highlight of any show.

DAVID SHANHUN

"Once in a while you see an artist who is out of the ordinary." - The Shirley Ryder Show

David Shanhun has opened for Rock legends Foreigner, & Heart, and has performed in NZ, Japan, Australia, and the UK. His exquisite guitar work shines under his superb storytelling and songwriting. He's performed with Grammy Award winner Bryan White, and is known for his engaging live shows and heartfelt tunes.

Expect an evening of unforgettable music, plenty of laughs, and the kind of connection that only comes from two great friends & musicians sharing the stage.

long_description:
🎵 Beautiful Chamber Music with a Magical View🎵 Comfy Concert🎻 Saturday 24 October, 4 - 6PM

Relax with a cuppa and enjoy exquisite live music from The Chamber Pot Pourri Ensemble & special guests!

The Comfy Concert on 24 October features Anna Gawn, mezzo soprano (formerly of the Kugels klezmer band), Anna van der Zee (violin), Nick Hancox (viola), Ross Harris (accordion), alongside Helene Pohl (violin) and Rolf Gjelsten (cello).This is a very special event  - a launch of new CD Moriamur and with performances by top classical musicians. The afternoon is headlined by a klezmer-inspired song-cycle for mezzo soprano and string quartet by Harris, along with a vivacious violin-cello duo by Erwin Schulhoff.

Two pieces composed by Ross Harris will be performed at the Comfy Concert in Roseneath on Saturday 24th. Harris, Arts Laureate and one of New Zealand's most revered and versatile composers, wrote both pieces specially for Anna Gawn, who will perform for us this afternoon! The first, is a world premiere of Moriamur for mezzo soprano and string quartet - a song cycle based on the story of doomed love of Dido and Aeneas, with words taken from the 4th Book of Virgil's The Aeneid. The second work (Songs for Dark Times) is a series of songs for mezzo soprano, string quartet and accordion, originally written for the klezmer group The Kugels.

Doors open from 3:30pm

Please join us early for light refreshment and to get comfy before the performance starts at 4.

id: Chapel Of Sound II-31 Avon Street, Island Bay, Wellington 6023, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Chapel Of Sound II
venue: 31 Avon Street, Island Bay, Wellington 6023, New Zealand
long_description:
Erskine Chapel in Island Bay is considered one of the finest examples of French-Gothic architecture in NZ. Built in 1929 and restored in the 1990s, it features an Italian marble interior, soaring, vaulted ceilings and world-renown acoustics. For the first time since Erskine was built, it reeled with the sound of the underground on July 25th this year. The full audiovisual experience was a night to remember, the energy was felt by everyone there, the dancefloor was packed from start to finish, it looked and sounded incredible. So we are doing the only thing we could do; we are making it happen all over again.

As before; expect projection mapped elements, lighting to knock you sideways, sound that soars, a fully licensed bar, a decked-out chill area, a dancefloor under the arches and a collection of some of Aotearoa’s favourite selectors who will have the chapel rocking.

Dylan C is a household name. His music journey began back in the day working at Cuba Street’s Real Groovy, before moving north and embarking on a seven-year residency at Tāmaki Makaurau’s fabled Rakinos.From there, Dylan became a cornerstone of the local scene, spending 10 years as Program Director at Base FM and 15 years running the Jungle Stage at Northern Bass. He’s played almost every event you can think of, from Electric Avenue and Tora Bombora to legendary late-night and closing sets at Splore.He’s also been the vibe controller behind Shipwrecked’s Hidden Reef Stage and remains a staple across the board on any lineup. His deep, clever cuts never fail to move a dancefloor - he’s a master of his craft.

Heylady was born in Wellington in the boiler room of Tatou in the 90s. She started promoting in the early 2000s, and by 2010 had picked up the DJ bug and was playing regularly alongside internationals and locals. A well recognised name in Aotearoa’s underground, she has played the length and breadth of the country, across Australia and America. She’s one of the founding members of Taniwha’s Den, she’s one half of COMMUNICATE and co-owner of XCOMMUNICATE records. With decades of collecting killer house and techno under her belt, her well-honed ear always makes for a stomping dancefloor.

Hape has been holding it down in Wellington since the late 90s. He’s had residencies at some of the city’s most recognised establishments, brought musicians together under multiple event brands and been one of the people who have kept the scene alive. His custom brand of rolling, soul-driven sound is instantly discernible, he has a current residency at Havana Bar, and is a regular at Taniwha’s Den, his closing set last time went down in the history books.

Nam Chucks is a DJ, selector and longtime radio host at Radioactive FM. She possesses a deep respect and appreciation for sound system philosophy, dedicating her musical selections to the concepts of unity and inclusion in rave culture. She is a believer in guiding the dance and has huge respect for all things sacred and indigenous. She has played for a huge variety of events in her time, and she always holds it down.

Lady Lazerlight knocked it out of the park with her projection mapping and light show last time, so we’ve brought her back for this round.

With all this and more, we recommend arriving early. The goodness starts when the doors open and we’d hate for you to miss any of the show. Tickets are extremely limited, we suggest grabbing yours before they are gone as last time they sold out in less than 48 hours.

IMPORTANT INFO: Our event is a safe space for all. If you or someone you know is feeling unsafe or harassed, please approach one of the bar staff or security. If you are behaving badly and impacting other’s ability to have a good time you will be removed. Please act with respect and care for your fellow attendees at all times, no means no and this goes for conversations as well as more intimate requests.

id: Global ChangeLabs: Breakfast w/ Banny Banerjee & co (WLG)-30 Waring Taylor Street, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Global ChangeLabs: Breakfast w/ Banny Banerjee & co (WLG)
venue: 30 Waring Taylor Street, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Designing Desirable Transformations in a Complex World

With Banny Banerjee and a panel of Aotearoa changemakers.

The challenges we face today; from technological disruption and climate change to organisational transformation and societal change... are increasingly complex, interconnected and difficult to solve through any single intervention.

So how do we design transformations in the context of complex, systemic, and interconnected challenges?

Join us for a special conversation with Banny Banerjee, founder of Global ChangeLabs and Adjunct Professor at Stanford University’s Doerr School of Sustainability.

Before launching Global ChangeLabs, Banny founded Stanford ChangeLabs and spent two decades working across fields and exploring how to approach complex and deeply integrated challenges and design genuinely transformative pathways. Earlier in his career, Banny worked at IDEO during the period when the firm was helping pioneer what became known as Design Thinking.

For this special event, Banny will share insights about how conventional wisdom and deterministic approaches are increasingly ill suited to address the deeply systemic and integrated nature of our challenges.  He will share how his work across sectors - business, government, technology, sustainability and social systems indicates the need for new capacities, leadership models, organizational functions, and platforms to address an uncertain and increasingly complex future.  Given his work on how to leverage a diversity of perspectives, we will also be joined by a panel of local change-makers to explore what these ideas might mean in the Aotearoa New Zealand context.

We’ll explore:

How do we embrace the complexity rather than expect isolated solutions to work?

How must we reframe design and innovation to shape interventions that shift the trajectory of a system?

How do we effectively combine different disciplines, perspectives and ways of thinking?

How do we identify opportunities for meaningful intervention and make them actionable?

What new forms of leadership, collaboration and organisational architecture might be needed for systemic transformation?

long_description:
Hailing from the music-filled streets of Melbourne, Australia, Shaun Kirk is an award-winning blues and soul troubadour recognised for his exceptional talent as a born entertainer. His unique talent has not only earned him many accolades but also much praise from fellow artists, such as three-time Grammy Award Winner Fantastic Negrito, who has declared his show as "One of the best one-man shows he’s ever seen!"

Kirk's vocals exude a gritty, soulful depth that seems to transcend far beyond his years, with critics continually acclaiming him as "one of the finest blues voices Australia has ever heard" (Buzz Mag). Complementing his vocal artistry, Kirk's vintage guitar tones and raw grooves pay tribute to the timeless influences that have shaped his musical journey, resulting in a distinctive sound fast becoming his own.

Shaun’s musical journey has taken him to stages all over the world, where he's not only performed but consistently sold out shows, leaving audiences enthralled by his magnetic presence. From iconic festival stages like Bluesfest Byron Bay, where he's become a familiar name, to sharing the billing with legends like Robert Plant of Led Zeppelin, John Mayer, Paolo Nutini, John Butler Trio, and The Teskey Brothers; Kirk's artistic prowess is in esteemed company. Moreover, he's also had the honour of opening for household names such as blues maestro Joe Bonamassa, soul sensation Allen Stone, and the indomitable Beth Hart; further solidifying his place in the landscape of contemporary music. This remarkable journey is a testament to Kirk's unmatched talent and ability to connect with audiences across genres and generations.

“It’s rare to see someone bring down the house as an opener, but Australia’s Shaun Kirk did exactly that. He connected with the crowd immediately” – Soundcheck Entertainment, Canada

“One of the most explosive acts Australia has to offer” – Mixdown Magazine, Australia

“Simply astounding." - Forte Magazine, Australia

long_description:
Power Up the Hutt – Central Lower Hutt

A more comfortable home. Lower energy bills. Greater peace of mind.

If you've been wondering whether electrification could make a real difference to your home and your household budget, this free community event is the perfect place to start.

Join us at Hutt Bowling Club, 6 bMyrtle Street on Thursday 29 October at 7:30 pm for an informative and welcoming evening where local people share how they've transformed the way they live.

From warmer homes in winter and lower running costs to cleaner indoor air and greater energy independence, electrification is helping Hutt Valley households enjoy a better quality of life while reducing their environmental impact.

You'll hear firsthand experiences from local residents who have installed heat pumps, solar panels, home batteries, electric hot water systems, induction cooktops and electric vehicles. They'll explain what motivated them, what the process was like, what they would do differently, and the benefits they're now enjoying every day.

Whether you're just beginning to explore your options or you're ready to take the next step, you'll leave with practical ideas, greater confidence, and a clearer understanding of where to begin.

This is a community event—not a sales presentation. There are no technical lectures or pressure to buy anything. Just honest conversations, practical advice, and the opportunity to ask questions in a relaxed and friendly setting.

Businesses, schools and community organisations interested in electrification are also welcome.

Free admission. Everyone welcome.

Come along and discover how simple changes today can create a home that's more comfortable, more affordable to run, and better prepared for the future.

id: Gong Bath with Hammocks!-6/149 Karori Road, Karori, Wellington 6012, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Gong Bath with Hammocks!
venue: 6/149 Karori Road, Karori, Wellington 6012, New Zealand
long_description:
Join Nick for his last therapeutic Gong Bath with your choice of hammock or floor seat, to soak in the vibrations and beautiful droning sounds of three medium-large Paiste 'Planet' gongs, Tibetan 'full moon' bowls, and medium sized sound therapy instruments.

The science behind these gongs baths are: the rich harmonics of the gongs invite your body and mind to rest into deeper brainwave states, and the drones invite the nervous system to relax because the long continuous sounds say 'things are moving slowly, this is safe'. The sounds themselves are like some kind of rich, harmonic, cosmic electronic music yet primal and organic. Nick uses three medium-large Paiste 'Planet' gongs, which are tuned to a fundamental pitch, and were developed specifically for sound therapy compared to some other gongs.

Nick has been producing and playing with music since his earliest teens, having graduated from The New Zealand School of Music, and The University of Auckland in Psychology with over 4 years of work experience in experiential therapies, combining musical and therapeutic worlds with events like these throughout Wellington and the lower North Island for the past 2.5+ years. He uses Somatic Psychology informed grounding practices at the beginning and end of the session

The Yoga Studio has ample free parking and easy access via Bus Route 2 at the Marsden Village stop. The studio is up the blue wooden staircase which you can see when you're in the carpark in the Masden Village. Please arrive 5ish minutes early, so we can start at 6pm for the grounding introduction.

Please bring along anything that'll help you feel more comfortable (blankets, pillows, and bolsters come with your ticket, but you can bring along eye masks, earplugs etc if you need that).

If you live with any of these, please talk to your Doctor first, to make sure the event will be suitable:

-have a pacemaker or other implanted medical device

-live with epilepsy or a sound-sensitive condition

-are in the first trimester of pregnancy

-are experiencing severe or unmanaged mental health challenges (such as psychosis, schizophrenia, or PTSD)

If you're trying to decide between the hammock or floor ticket, the hammock is better for slightly shorter people (under 5"8), while the floor is good for people who like to stretch out more.

See you there!

long_description:
Hungary 1956–2026: 70 Years On

An evening of conversation, film and Hungarian hospitality

Join us at the Penthouse Cinema as we begin three days of events in Wellington commemorating the 70th anniversary of the 1956 Hungarian Revolution and Freedom Fight.

The evening opens with Hungarian nibbles and wine, followed by a panel discussion reflecting on the meaning and legacy of 1956 – revolution, freedom, resistance, displacement and the experience of starting again in a new country.

Panellists: Chris Finlayson, Alan Duff, Zoya Kőszegi and István Tóth
Moderator: Zsófia Hellyer

The discussion will be followed by a screening of the acclaimed Hungarian film Children of Glory (Szabadság, szerelem), set against the dramatic events of the 1956 Revolution and the Melbourne Olympic Games.

The film is in Hungarian with English subtitles.

Come for the whole evening or choose the parts of the programme you would like to attend.

Everyone is welcome – you don't need to be Hungarian or have any prior knowledge of the 1956 Revolution.

id: America After Trump: What will it mean for Asia and the World?-Hunter Building Kelburn Parade, Kelburn, Wellington 6012, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: America After Trump: What will it mean for Asia and the World?
venue: Hunter Building Kelburn Parade, Kelburn, Wellington 6012, New Zealand
long_description:
With the U.S. midterm elections just around the corner, the race to replace Donald Trump is just about to kick off. In this lecture, one of the sharpest observers of contemporary American foreign policy, Zack Cooper, will discuss how the American approach to foreign policy is changing and explore what a post-Trump world view might mean for Asia in particular.

Zack Cooper is a senior fellow at the American Enterprise Institute, where he studies US strategy in Asia, including alliance dynamics and US-China competition. He also teaches at Princeton University. He previously worked at the National Security Council and in the Office of the Secretary of Defense. Dr. Cooper is the author of Tides of Fortune: The Rise and Decline of Great Militaries from Yale University Press. He has also co-authored books, reports, and articles on US strategy and alliances in Asia. His writing has appeared in academic journals and popular press, including International Security, Security Studies, Foreign Affairs, the New York Times, the Washington Post, and the Wall Street Journal, among other outlets. Dr. Cooper graduated from Princeton University with a PhD and an MA in security studies and an MPA in international relations. He received a BA in public policy from Stanford University.

Refreshments will be provid at the event.

Ange and The Boss tells the improbable story of all-time great Hungarian footballer Ferenc Puskás finding himself in Melbourne in the late 80s, coaching the Greek NSL team South Melbourne Hellas.

Barely able to speak English and comedically overweight, he united and inspired the team to a dramatic championship win in 1991. Eating, drinking, and enjoying himself along the way.

About the Liner Shipping Game

The Liner Shipping Game is a cutting-edge, simulation-based training solution that provides hands-on insights into the intricacies of liner shipping operations. It simplifies real-world processes, making it suitable for both industry newcomers and seasoned professionals.

Participants navigate realistic, customisable scenarios reflecting operational disruptions, key decision points, and challenges.

Key features include:

Booking Uptake: Manage dynamic booking requests while balancing capacity constraints and customer expectations.

Vessel Stowage: Plan and optimise vessel space, considering cargo types, weight distribution, and voyage schedules.

Terminal Operations: Coordinate port activities, manage container flows, and ensure efficient cargo handling.

The game's interactive nature provides practical experience and enhances skills in teamwork, revenue management, and process optimisation

.

For a closer look at the LinerGame experience, watch our official highlight video on YouTube.

Why Attend?

The Liner Shipping Game offers a rare opportunity to learn from top-tier industry experts while collaborating with peers from across the logistics sector. By attending, you will:

Understand Complex Operations: Experience the decision-making process of running a liner shipping service, covering end-to-end operations.

Enhance Your Skills: Improve your teamwork, strategic thinking, and revenue management capabilities in a fast-paced, risk-free environment.

Navigate Real-World Scenarios: Encounter challenges like port strikes, equipment shortages, weather disruptions, and overlapping booking regions, gaining critical insights into effective problem-solving.

Network with Industry Peers: Connect with like-minded professionals in a collaborative setting, exchange ideas, and explore new opportunities within the shipping and logistics sector.

Who Should Attend?

This workshop is ideal for:

Logistics & Supply Chain Professionals: Individuals involved in operations, planning, and management.

Importers & Exporters: Professionals managing supply chain activities and interested in gaining a broader understanding of liner shipping dynamics.

Freight Forwarders & Shippers: Those seeking to enhance their service offerings by understanding carrier operations better.

Port & Terminal Operators: Professionals responsible for terminal management and coordination.

CLUEDUNNIT

DINNER WITH 'MURDER ON THE MENU'

Step into a world of intrigue, suspense, and unforgettable entertainment as InterContinental Wellington partners with Cluedunnit to present an immersive murder mystery dining experience. Guests will be transported into a captivating story where secrets unfold, clues emerge, and every guest becomes part of the investigation.

Combining exceptional hospitality with live theatrical entertainment, Cluedunnit invites guests to enjoy a delicious dining experience while questioning suspects, following leads, and working together to solve a thrilling mystery. From the moment you arrive, you'll be immersed in a world of drama, laughter, and unexpected twists.

Whether you're planning a unique night out with friends, celebrating a special occasion, or enjoying an unforgettable evening with colleagues, Cluedunnit at InterContinental Wellington promises the perfect blend of fine dining, mystery, and entertainment.

Guests will interact with a live cast of characters, uncover clues, and work together to crack the case, all while enjoying a delicious three-course dinner.

But beware, all is not as it seems. As secrets unravel and tensions rise, you'll need to decipher the clues, question the suspects, and piece together the evidence before it's too late. After all, where there's a will, there's a murder.

Where there's a mystery, there's a motive. Where there's a motive, there's a murder. The question is: whodunnit?

MURDER AT THE MANOR - The Story So Far...

It is 1929 and this English Cotswold beauty spot is celebrating the life of elderly heiress Rose Stimper, who, in an act of philanthropy, has bequeathed the village a large sum of money and left instructions that the villagers must decide how best to spend it. 

This will be a party like no other. Everyone has ideas on how to spend the money, and the entire village turns out to attend Pokeingham Hall, which has been thrown open for the first time in many years to host the event.

But beware, all is not as it seems. There are dark forces at work.

Enjoy a delicious three course dinner as you question the suspects, decipher the clues and work to crack the case. And please remember - where there’s a will, there’s a murder!

id: The Lady’s Not for Burning-106 Cashmere Avenue, Khandallah, Wellington 6035, New Zealand  ·  Accessibility info-Humanitix
name: The Lady’s Not for Burning
venue: 106 Cashmere Avenue, Khandallah, Wellington 6035, New Zealand  ·  Accessibility info
long_description:
The Lady's Not for Burning will entrance you with its sparkling humour, witty wordplay, poetic lyricism, satisfying love stories and occasional excoriations of the follies of humankind.

Will world-weary discharged soldier Thomas Mendip achieve his desire for death by hanging?

Who will sweet young convent-raised Alizon Eliot marry - the stuffy older brother or the impetuous younger one? Or neither?

Will the Mayor and the Justice of the small market-town of Cool Clary really give in to the mob and burn as a witch the vivacious and spirited Jennet Jourdemayne in the morning?

The Lady's Not for Burning, set in "1400, either more or less or exactly", is one of Christofer Fry's most well-known works. First performed in 1948, its life-affirming post-war optimism was an instant success with audiences and critics alike. Today, its humour and delightful storytelling are just as enjoyably satisfying as they were then.

This is a community theatre production by special arrangement with Concord Theatricals and The Play Bureau.
