id: Global ChangeLabs: Breakfast w/ Banny Banerjee & co (WLG)-30 Waring Taylor Street, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Global ChangeLabs: Breakfast w/ Banny Banerjee & co (WLG)
venue: 30 Waring Taylor Street, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Designing Desirable Transformations in a Complex World

With Banny Banerjee and a panel of Aotearoa changemakers.

The challenges we face today; from technological disruption and climate change to organisational transformation and societal change... are increasingly complex, interconnected and difficult to solve through any single intervention.

So how do we design transformations in the context of complex, systemic, and interconnected challenges?

Join us for a special conversation with Banny Banerjee, founder of Global ChangeLabs and Adjunct Professor at Stanford University’s Doerr School of Sustainability.

Before launching Global ChangeLabs, Banny founded Stanford ChangeLabs and spent two decades working across fields and exploring how to approach complex and deeply integrated challenges and design genuinely transformative pathways. Earlier in his career, Banny worked at IDEO during the period when the firm was helping pioneer what became known as Design Thinking.

For this special event, Banny will share insights about how conventional wisdom and deterministic approaches are increasingly ill suited to address the deeply systemic and integrated nature of our challenges.  He will share how his work across sectors - business, government, technology, sustainability and social systems indicates the need for new capacities, leadership models, organizational functions, and platforms to address an uncertain and increasingly complex future.  Given his work on how to leverage a diversity of perspectives, we will also be joined by a panel of local change-makers to explore what these ideas might mean in the Aotearoa New Zealand context.

We’ll explore:

How do we embrace the complexity rather than expect isolated solutions to work?

How must we reframe design and innovation to shape interventions that shift the trajectory of a system?

How do we effectively combine different disciplines, perspectives and ways of thinking?

How do we identify opportunities for meaningful intervention and make them actionable?

What new forms of leadership, collaboration and organisational architecture might be needed for systemic transformation?

How might Aotearoa NZ become a place to demonstrate transformative ways of approaching complex challenges.  What can Aotearoa NZ contribute and learn... Especially, as we navigate our own economic, technological, environmental and societal transitions?

This will be an opportunity to hear a distinctive international perspective, connect it with the experiences of people working on complex challenges here in Aotearoa, and consider what it might mean to design the conditions for a different future.

Who is this for?

Anyone working to create meaningful change in complex environments: including leaders, designers, strategists, innovators, entrepreneurs, policymakers, researchers, funders, social-sector practitioners and people working across organisational and sector boundaries.

Come curious.

Bring a complex challenge.

Leave with new perspectives on where, and how, change might be possible.

We'd love for you to join us for this breakfast event, to explore how we can Designing Desirable Transformations in a Complex World

🔹 Date & Time: Wednesday 28 October 2026, 8 - 9:30am
🔹 Location: Precinct Flex, 30 Waring Taylor St (Te Whanganui ā Tara / Wellington NZ)
🔹 Registration: $20 unwaged | $45 waged (To cover venue hire, coffee, tea & breakfast pastries)

Ngā manaakitanga | We look forward to seeing you there!

long_description:
Since the release of Fruit Fly earlier this year, the novel has soared up bestseller lists around the world and been optioned for a TV series, cementing Josh Silver as one of the hottest voices in contemporary fiction.

Seven years ago, Mallory became a literary sensation. Now, after years of writer's block, she's determined to revive her career before it fades into obscurity. Desperate for a hit, she turns to Reddit for advice on writing a bestseller: go gay, go sad, go dark. When she meets Leo, a young queer man struggling with addiction, she begins writing his story, without his knowledge. But how far is she willing to go in pursuit of the perfect novel?

Join Josh Silver for a captivating evening discussing Fruit Fly, his engrossing new novel that explores ambition, identity and the ethics of telling other people's stories, in-conversation with curator and writer Tendai Mutambu.

Order your copy of Josh Silver’s novel, Fruit Fly, at Unity Books Wellington, who will be bookselling at this event.

This project is supported by the British Council New Zealand and the Pacific.

long_description:
The trustees of Blue Dragon Children's Trust NZ warmly invite you to our annual fundraising film. The film we have chosen is KLARA AND THE SUN. Directed by Taika Waititi, the story is based on Kazuo Ishiguro’s accalimed novel.

What it's about:

It follows Klara, an Artificial Friend - chosen by a young girl named Josie to join her family. It's a thoughtful and emotional story exploring love, loneliness, hope and what it means to be human in our AI-driven world. The themes of AI ethics and human relationships make it great viewing for families with teenagers (M rating).

All the money we raise goes to Blue Dragon Children's Foundation in Hanoi, which works to break the poverty cycle for Vietnam's poorest children, including street kids, children with disabilities, and victims of human trafficking and slavery.

Tickets:

$25 a ticket or $30 a ticket, which includes a raffle ticket. As always, there will be at least two raffles with delicious home-made Christmas cakes and other goodies. Please bring plenty of cash on the night to buy extra raffle tickets and increase your chances of being a lucky winner.

long_description:
Well Ahead: Put your health on the agenda

An event for women balancing demanding careers, businesses and families, who are already invested in their health and want to understand it more deeply.

As energy, sleep, recovery and body composition shift through midlife, the right information matters.

Well Ahead brings together Dame Susan Devoy and a lineup of experts across health, nutrition, movement and healthy ageing to explore the science and strategy behind:

Energy and recovery

Sleep and stress

Nutrition

Strength and movement

Body composition

Hormonal changes

Perimenopause and menopause

Bone health

Genetics and individual biology

Well Ahead is designed as a connected conversation, not a series of standalone talks.

Each speaker builds on the last, giving you a clearer, more complete picture of your own health rather than a list of disconnected tips.

The day opens with an optional workshop, Your Genes, Your Choices, exploring genetics, DNA testing and the role our genes can play in understanding individual biology. The full programme continues into the afternoon and closes with a live panel and audience Q&A.

Practical information. Expert perspectives. One day, properly invested in your health.

Choose a Morning Workshop pass, Main Event pass, or the Full Pass for the whole day.




Click here to find out more.



“Women spend so much of their lives looking after everyone and everything else. Well Ahead is about putting your own health on the agenda, hearing from people who really know their field, and coming away with information and ideas you can actually use. You don't have to have all the answers. Sometimes you just need to make the time to start asking the right questions.”

- Dame Susan Devoy

Well Ahead is supported by a growing network of organisations across Wellington's business, professional, health, fitness and wellness communities, all helping us bring women together for an important conversation about health through midlife.

About Conquer Health

Conquer Health helps men and women understand their unique biology, so they can focus on what matters to their health today and make informed choices for the years ahead. Rather than one-size-fits-all health advice, Conquer Health combines advanced biological testing with a multidisciplinary clinical team to build a personalised picture of your health, delivered remotely anywhere in New Zealand.

long_description:
TEQ Talks Wellington | Thursday 29 October 2026 | From 6:00pm

Victoria University of Wellington – Te Aro Campus, LT1
139 Vivian Street, Wellington

TEQ Talks is back in Wellington with another evening of short, sharp talks from fascinating people about the things they’re most passionate about, across VFX, art, science, culture, and beyond.

This edition brings together four very different perspectives — from delivering feature-grade VFX from a boutique Wellington studio, to sculpting dragons, creative technology and the arrival of MDMA-assisted therapy in Aotearoa New Zealand.

Four speakers. Four different perspectives. One evening of ideas, creativity and conversation.

Join us from 6:00pm for drinks, nibbles and networking, with talks kicking off at 7:00pm.

Speakers

Scott Chambers | Founder & Senior VFX Supervisor, 808 Ltd

Punching Above Our Weight: VFX from a Boutique NZ Floor

How a small Wellington studio ships feature-grade visual effects without a Hollywood machine behind it and what that means for craft, crew and clients.

Scott Chambers is Founder and Senior VFX Supervisor at 808 Ltd, a Wellington boutique studio delivering feature and episodic VFX.

Kim Beaton | Sculptor

Making the World, One Dragon at a Time

The story behind the creation of a universal sculpting material, Pal Tiya Premium.

Kim Beaton is a veteran sculptor of 30 years and a passionate advocate of magic realism in sculpture.

Dr G | Psychiatrist

MDMA-Assisted Therapy Has Arrived in Aotearoa New Zealand! Or: Can Psychedelics Change the World?

MDMA-assisted therapy has been approved in New Zealand for two psychiatrists. What is MDMA-assisted therapy, and what could its arrival mean for Aotearoa New Zealand?

Dr G is a consultant psychiatrist, professor of psychiatry and neuroscience, author and researcher with a passion for psychedelic therapies. He is one of the first two doctors in New Zealand approved to prescribe MDMA.

Delainy Jamahl | Creative Director, Artificial Imagination & Co-Founder, The Grid

Solving Problems with Creative Technology

Delainy works at the intersection of art and technology, leveraging technology to create art that moves while developing new techniques and tools to solve problems throughout the creative process.

Event Details

6:00pm – Drinks, nibbles and networking
7:00pm – TEQ Talks begin
9:00pm – Talks wrap
From around 9:30pm – Continue the conversation at Havana till late

Drinks and nibbles will be provided at Vic Uni.

Tickets

FREE – VES members
FREE – VFXG members
FREE – Victoria University of Wellington students
$10 – Students (non-members)
$20 – Professionals (non-members)

Spaces are limited and TEQ Talks does sell out, so grab your ticket early.

TEQ Talks Wellington is presented in partnership with the Visual Effects Society New Zealand Chapter, VFX Professionals Guild and Victoria University of Wellington.

long_description:
04butchclub presents SAPPHIC SESSION - a night showcasing some local sapphic and FLINTA* talent of Te Whanganui-a-Tara.

Why We're Here

Live music hits differently when you're surrounded by your community so it's about time this happens for Te Whanganui-a-Tara sapphic/FLINTA* scene. In this dedicated FLINTA* space, you will be serenaded by incredibly talented musicians and artists based in Te Whanganui-a-Tara.

As a bonus reason to party, this space was created to honour International Lesbian Day - a global celebration with deep local roots believed to have kicked off right here in Te Whanganui-a-Tara back in the 1980s!

Introducing: The Mad Butches (2026 'Make a Band' Project)

To shake things up and get talent back on stage, 04butchclub launched a 'make a band' project. In true community spirit, we gathered a group of keen singers and musicians - who haven't performed in a hot minute and had never met each other before - straight into a practice room. They've decided to be known as The Mad Butches, and maybe there's a good reason for it? Come witness the raw, collaborative magic of their very first live set!

What to expect on the night:

Open mic karaoke in the first 30min, or grab the guitar and sing a song as everyone filters in and settles into the scene.

An epic lineup - please see below for artists involved.

A couple of pool tables.

A chill, seated area for when you need to take a breather.

A table where you can enrol to vote, if you haven't already.

Timeline:

7.00pm - Doors open and open mic - choose your poison: karaoke or with guitar

7.30pm - Slam poetry from Lo

7.50pm - Comet

8.20pm - Danica Bryant

9.05pm - Mad Butches

10.05pm - Gift Horse

11.00pm - Event finish

Accessibility inside the venue:

Single-level access throughout the main venue except for the VIP area, which is up a flight of stairs.

Flashing lights (from stage and photographers) and loud sounds will be present.

Free foam earplugs will be available all night.

Important:

This is a no TERFs, no SWERFs space, and consent is mandatory. Visible event kaitiaki will be present and moving throughout the venue to help ensure everyone feels safe, respected, and supported. There will be campus security outside of the venue.

This event has been organised and will be run by volunteers. Ticket sales go towards covering the venue, equipment and paying the artists. Any profit made will go towards the following Sapphic Session 🔥👀

Celebrate, connect and be inspired as we bring the Wellington Women in HealthTech community together to close out 2026.

Join us for an evening of conversation, connection and festive celebration, featuring a panel discussion with Kelsey Schwynn and Eileen Duddy from Health New Zealand | Te Whatu Ora Digital Services. Her career has included supporting government agencies, not-for-profits and Fortune 500 companies through human-centred design, product strategy and large-scale digital change.

Eileen Duddy is a strategic digital health leader with more than 20 years’ experience in the health sector, including over a decade working across complex, cross-government initiatives. As a Digital Health Partner at Health New Zealand | Te Whatu Ora, she connects Digital Services with health sector stakeholders, translating clinical, operational and strategic priorities into aligned digital roadmaps and investment pathways. long_description:
An afternoon of exploratory improvisations and new compositions at Karori's Futuna Chapel. Doors open at 2pm, music starts 2:30pm.



Doxing Ur Mum is a new song cycle composed by Mallory Elmo, with lyrics by poet and textile artist Anne Amber, performed by Kassandra Wang (mezzo-soprano) and Antonia Grant (violin). 

The fruit of three years of collaboration, these songs speak aphoristically of everyday, intimate, and queer personal experiences in the city of Pōneke. Kassandra and Antonia will also perform a new work by Ōtautahi-based composer Luka Reardon and a collaborative composition of their own.



Multifaceted musicians lucky pollock, Amy-Jane, and Tristan Carter will join forces on flute, violin, keyboard, and more, exploring ambient free improvisation through their shared classical, popular, and experimental backgrounds. 

scramble204, Shay Patel (guitar)'s project with Vinnie Whitehead (guitar) and Alex Hoare (cello), will present an iteration of their Dialogues series.



Presented by Swamp Soul and Pyramid Club Offsite

Poster design by Shay Patel

Fresh off the release of their debut EP "The New Spring", ISKRA are coming to Superfina for two sets of high energy horn led jazz and dance music.

long_description:
TEQ Talks Wellington | Thursday 29 October 2026 | From 6:00pm

Victoria University of Wellington – Te Aro Campus, LT1
139 Vivian Street, Wellington

TEQ Talks is back in Wellington with another evening of short, sharp talks from fascinating people about the things they’re most passionate about, across VFX, art, science, culture, and beyond.

This edition brings together four very different perspectives — from delivering feature-grade VFX from a boutique Wellington studio, to sculpting dragons, creative technology and the arrival of MDMA-assisted therapy in Aotearoa New Zealand.

Four speakers. Four different perspectives. One evening of ideas, creativity and conversation.

Join us from 6:00pm for drinks, nibbles and networking, with talks kicking off at 7:00pm.

Speakers

Scott Chambers | Founder & Senior VFX Supervisor, 808 Ltd

Punching Above Our Weight: VFX from a Boutique NZ Floor

How a small Wellington studio ships feature-grade visual effects without a Hollywood machine behind it and what that means for craft, crew and clients.

Scott Chambers is Founder and Senior VFX Supervisor at 808 Ltd, a Wellington boutique studio delivering feature and episodic VFX.

Kim Beaton | Sculptor

Making the World, One Dragon at a Time

The story behind the creation of a universal sculpting material, Pal Tiya Premium.

Kim Beaton is a veteran sculptor of 30 years and a passionate advocate of magic realism in sculpture.

Dr G | Psychiatrist

MDMA-Assisted Therapy Has Arrived in Aotearoa New Zealand! Or: Can Psychedelics Change the World?

MDMA-assisted therapy has been approved in New Zealand for two psychiatrists. What is MDMA-assisted therapy, and what could its arrival mean for Aotearoa New Zealand?

Dr G is a consultant psychiatrist, professor of psychiatry and neuroscience, author and researcher with a passion for psychedelic therapies. He is one of the first two doctors in New Zealand approved to prescribe MDMA.

Delainy Jamahl | Creative Director, Artificial Imagination & Co-Founder, The Grid

Solving Problems with Creative Technology

Delainy works at the intersection of art and technology, leveraging technology to create art that moves while developing new techniques and tools to solve problems throughout the creative process.

Event Details

6:00pm – Drinks, nibbles and networking
7:00pm – TEQ Talks begin
9:00pm – Talks wrap
From around 9:30pm – Continue the conversation at Havana till late

Drinks and nibbles will be provided at Vic Uni.

Tickets

FREE – VES members
FREE – VFXG members
FREE – Victoria University of Wellington students
$10 – Students (non-members)
$20 – Professionals (non-members)

Spaces are limited and TEQ Talks does sell out, so grab your ticket early.

TEQ Talks Wellington is presented in partnership with the Visual Effects Society New Zealand Chapter, VFX Professionals Guild and Victoria University of Wellington.

venue: 20 Customhouse Quay, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Life and health insurance: rethinking the model

Customer expectations, product design, underwriting, claims and advice are all moving faster than traditional operating models can keep up with. At the same time, insurers are rethinking traditional products to meet the evolving needs of more New Zealanders, regulatory reform and a tough economic climate. That pressure is pushing insurers to rethink how they're built and to find new ways to support customers in sustainable ways.

Join the InsurTech community in Wellington on 12th November to hear how life and health insurers are innovating.

In the lead up to the launch of Acenda Life in New Zealand in 2027, we’ll hear what has been learned by Asteron Life following their exit from Suncorp and acquisition by Resolution Life Australasia with a further ownership structure to being a member of the Nippon Life Group.  The presentation will further focus on learnings from a digital, data and customer experience perspective.

Then a panel of insurance and insurtech leaders will look at the big issues and trends shaping the sector into 2027. They'll cover how AI is being used in practice today, the opportunities Open Data could open up, and what makes partnerships between insurers and insurtechs work. Hear from Asteron Life, Deloitte, Life Direct, Monvia, Partners Life and Simfuni.

Register now to attend this event and connect with insurance and data professionals. Generously supported by Deloitte and Asteron Life.


Date: 12 November 2026

Time:  5:00PM - 7.00PM

Location: Deloitte's offices, 20 Customhouse Quay.

long_description:
“breathtaking mastery of intent, understanding and execution throughout” – Middle C

After a highly successful Auckland/Northland tour the Korimako Trio are back in Wellington with a new programme.    

The Korimako Trio (Helene Pohl, violin; Rolf Gjelsten, cello; Michael Endres, piano) brings together three internationally renowned musicians with decades of experience who are beloved in New Zealand for their powerful communication as well as the intelligence of their playing.

In this concert they bring you music ranging from Zemlinsky's Trio, opus 3 ("the epitome of 1890s Vienna: lush, grand, romantic, impassioned") to the exuberance of Chopin's Introduction and Polonaise brilliante (cello and piano), and Janacek 's dramatic Sonata for violin and piano.

The programme closes by returning to the composer who established the piano trio as a genre. Haydn's Trio in A major crowns the evening with luminous grace, wit and a joyful affirmation of music's power to delight.

id: One Day Secular Meditation Retreat in Wellington-31 Lawson Place, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: One Day Secular Meditation Retreat in Wellington
venue: 31 Lawson Place, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
We know from ancient wisdom and modern psychology that meditation brings many benefits for our mental and physical wellbeing. It can reduce worry and pain, and improve calmness, focus, sleep, relationships and life satisfaction. The more time we spend meditating, and the more skilled we become, the greater the benefits.

So take a restorative break from your daily life, meet other meditators, and strengthen your practice at this small-group Sunday retreat. Everyone is welcome, whatever their level of meditation experience or preferred style. The retreat is beginner-friendly, and our approach is secular (meaning non-religious) which makes room for diverse beliefs.

The programme

We will begin with introductions, followed by a guided meditation that covers the core skills of both sitting and walking meditation. For the rest of the day, the meditation will be unguided apart from occasional bells to announce breaks, and to remind you to alternate between sitting and walking (if that's what you choose to do).

To help quieten the mind, many participants prefer not to talk again until the discussion circle at the end of the retreat. However some people like to chat with others during the breaks, and there is space allocated for this. The retreat leaders are always available for quiet conversations if you need support with your practice.

The venue

The Innermost Gardens hall is nestled between the central city suburb of Mount Victoria and the green town belt. This provides a peaceful nature-rich setting for the retreat, surrounded by community gardens to enjoy during the breaks or walking meditation.

There will be hot drinks and snacks available throughout the day. For lunch the participants bring a plate of vegetarian food to share. The venue has a full kitchen including cutlery, plates, bowls, fridge, stove, and a microwave.

The leaders

Bryan Royds is an adult educator and registered counsellor with a passion for wellbeing science and leadership development. He has been meditating and teaching meditation skills in groups for many years, including the well-researched methods of Mindfulness Based Stress Reduction (MBSR).

Sarah Jane Barnett is a writer and creative writing teacher at Massey University. She has been a Buddhist for ten years, practicing mostly Vipassana meditation. She also co-facilitates a meditation group for people who practice Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (an evidence-based modern psychotherapy and wellbeing method).

The registration fee is only $40 for waged and $20 for unwaged, fully refundable until one day prior.

id: Welcome Space Brothers - The Extraordinary True Story of the Unarius Academy of Science-93 Mornington Road, Brooklyn, Wellington 6021, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Welcome Space Brothers - The Extraordinary True Story of the Unarius Academy of Science
venue: 93 Mornington Road, Brooklyn, Wellington 6021, New Zealand
long_description:
WELCOME SPACE BROTHERS is a documentary that dives into the extraordinary true story of the Unarius Academy of Science, an extraterrestrial-channeling spiritual school founded in El Cajon in the 1970s. Led by the dazzlingly outlandish Ruth E. Norman—revered as "Archangel Uriel"—Unarius evolved into a wildly inventive public-access television phenomenon. The group produced films that appeared to be elaborately campy space epics yet were, at their core, sincere therapeutic works. 

From The Source Family director Jodi Wille comes another mind-expanding voyage into the wild frontiers of American belief, bringing her singular blend of empathy, humor, and emotional insight to one of the country's most fascinating outsider communities. Produced by Caryn Capotosto (Won’t You Be My Neighbor) and Jodi Wille. Executive producers include Elijah Wood, Moby, and Oscar-winning filmmakers Phil Lord and Christopher Miller.

Please join us for the Wellington screening of WELCOME SPACE BROTHERS - brought to you by Erika Grant and Night Church Cinema. This is a dress up event - come dressed in your favorite UFO/Cult fit. There will be prizes for best dressed, and DJ's Oona Verse and Martyn Pepperell plus others will guide us into the wild starry night with space cult inspired dance tracks.

The bar and restaurant will be open for dinner and drinks. This is a one off event, not to be missed!!

“Wild and Very Trippy” - Jodi Wille

“If I didn’t know Jodi Wille’s film, Welcome Space Brothers, was a documentary, I’d swear it was a WTF, insane, sci-fi tale of weirdness. The story of Ruth is fascinating…..” - Alan NG, Film Threat 

“It’s a vision of healing, acceptance, peace, cooperation, and hope, expressed through an outpouring of unbridled creative energy. If that spells crazy, beam me up!” — Doug Harvey, Artillery

id: America After Trump: What will it mean for Asia and the World?-Hunter Building Kelburn Parade, Kelburn, Wellington 6012, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: America After Trump: What will it mean for Asia and the World?
venue: Hunter Building Kelburn Parade, Kelburn, Wellington 6012, New Zealand
long_description:
With the U.S. midterm elections just around the corner, the race to replace Donald Trump is just about to kick off. In this lecture, one of the sharpest observers of contemporary American foreign policy, Zack Cooper, will discuss how the American approach to foreign policy is changing and explore what a post-Trump world view might mean for Asia in particular.

Zack Cooper is a senior fellow at the American Enterprise Institute, where he studies US strategy in Asia, including alliance dynamics and US-China competition. He also teaches at Princeton University. He previously worked at the National Security Council and in the Office of the Secretary of Defense. Dr. Cooper is the author of Tides of Fortune: The Rise and Decline of Great Militaries from Yale University Press. He has also co-authored books, reports, and articles on US strategy and alliances in Asia. His writing has appeared in academic journals and popular press, including International Security, Security Studies, Foreign Affairs, the New York Times, the Washington Post, and the Wall Street Journal, among other outlets. Dr. Cooper graduated from Princeton University with a PhD and an MA in security studies and an MPA in international relations. He received a BA in public policy from Stanford University.

Refreshments will be provid at the event.

id: One Day Secular Meditation Retreat in Wellington-31 Lawson Place, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: One Day Secular Meditation Retreat in Wellington
venue: 31 Lawson Place, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
We know from ancient wisdom and modern psychology that meditation brings many benefits for our mental and physical wellbeing. It can reduce worry and pain, and improve calmness, focus, sleep, relationships and life satisfaction. The more time we spend meditating, and the more skilled we become, the greater the benefits.

So take a restorative break from your daily life, meet other meditators, and strengthen your practice at this small-group Sunday retreat. Everyone is welcome, whatever their level of meditation experience or preferred style. The retreat is beginner-friendly, and our approach is secular (meaning non-religious) which makes room for diverse beliefs.

The programme

We will begin with introductions, followed by a guided meditation that covers the core skills of both sitting and walking meditation. For the rest of the day, the meditation will be unguided apart from occasional bells to announce breaks, and to remind you to alternate between sitting and walking (if that's what you choose to do).

To help quieten the mind, many participants prefer not to talk again until the discussion circle at the end of the retreat. However some people like to chat with others during the breaks, and there is space allocated for this. The retreat leaders are always available for quiet conversations if you need support with your practice.

The venue

The Innermost Gardens hall is nestled between the central city suburb of Mount Victoria and the green town belt. This provides a peaceful nature-rich setting for the retreat, surrounded by community gardens to enjoy during the breaks or walking meditation.

There will be hot drinks and snacks available throughout the day. For lunch the participants bring a plate of vegetarian food to share. The venue has a full kitchen including cutlery, plates, bowls, fridge, stove, and a microwave.

The leaders

Bryan Royds is an adult educator and registered counsellor with a passion for wellbeing science and leadership development. He has been meditating and teaching meditation skills in groups for many years, including the well-researched methods of Mindfulness Based Stress Reduction (MBSR).

Sarah Jane Barnett is a writer and creative writing teacher at Massey University. She has been a Buddhist for ten years, practicing mostly Vipassana meditation. She also co-facilitates a meditation group for people who practice Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (an evidence-based modern psychotherapy and wellbeing method).

The registration fee is only $40 for waged and $20 for unwaged, fully refundable until one day prior.

Moderator: Zsófia Hellyer

Everyone is welcome – you don't need to be Hungarian or have any prior knowledge of the 1956 Revolution.

id: Welcome Space Brothers - The Extraordinary True Story of the Unarius Academy of Science-93 Mornington Road, Brooklyn, Wellington 6021, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Welcome Space Brothers - The Extraordinary True Story of the Unarius Academy of Science
venue: 93 Mornington Road, Brooklyn, Wellington 6021, New Zealand
long_description:
WELCOME SPACE BROTHERS is a documentary that dives into the extraordinary true story of the Unarius Academy of Science, an extraterrestrial-channeling spiritual school founded in El Cajon in the 1970s. Led by the dazzlingly outlandish Ruth E. Norman—revered as "Archangel Uriel"—Unarius evolved into a wildly inventive public-access television phenomenon. The group produced films that appeared to be elaborately campy space epics yet were, at their core, sincere therapeutic works. 

From The Source Family director Jodi Wille comes another mind-expanding voyage into the wild frontiers of American belief, bringing her singular blend of empathy, humor, and emotional insight to one of the country's most fascinating outsider communities. Produced by Caryn Capotosto (Won’t You Be My Neighbor) and Jodi Wille. Executive producers include Elijah Wood, Moby, and Oscar-winning filmmakers Phil Lord and Christopher Miller.

Please join us for the Wellington screening of WELCOME SPACE BROTHERS - brought to you by Erika Grant and Night Church Cinema. This is a dress up event - come dressed in your favorite UFO/Cult fit. There will be prizes for best dressed, and DJ's Oona Verse and Martyn Pepperell plus others will guide us into the wild starry night with space cult inspired dance tracks.

The bar and restaurant will be open for dinner and drinks. This is a one off event, not to be missed!!

“Wild and Very Trippy” - Jodi Wille

“If I didn’t know Jodi Wille’s film, Welcome Space Brothers, was a documentary, I’d swear it was a WTF, insane, sci-fi tale of weirdness. The story of Ruth is fascinating…..” - Alan NG, Film Threat 

“It’s a vision of healing, acceptance, peace, cooperation, and hope, expressed through an outpouring of unbridled creative energy. If that spells crazy, beam me up!” — Doug Harvey, Artillery

id: Darren Watson Plays The Shed-46a Victoria Street, Alicetown, Lower Hutt 5010, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Darren Watson Plays The Shed
venue: 46a Victoria Street, Alicetown, Lower Hutt 5010, New Zealand
long_description:
Much-loved Pōneke blues and roots singer-songwriter Darren Watson is returning to his favourite Lower Hutt intimate venue, The Shed for the third time (with special guest Matt Hay).

For this visit the ex-Chicago Smoke Shop leader, ‘Planet Key’ songwriter, and multiple NZ Music Award nominee is bringing his musical compardre Matt Hay along to both open the show and accompany Watson on harmonica.

Watson’s latest album ‘Darren Watson sings John Hiatt’ was released just over a year ago to critical acclaim, including a 4-star review in US jazz and blues ‘bible’ Downbeat, and spectacular NZ chart success.

Opener Matt Hay’s latest album ‘Dog and Pony Show’ (produced by Watson) was judged ‘Best Americana Album’ at the 2024 Aotearoa NZ Folk Alliance Awards.

“ Matt brings his beautiful songs to open the show and then joins me blowing some beautiful, tasteful harp. I’m really enjoying playing with Matt again.”

Darren says this show, while still featuring a few choice Hiatt covers, will feature more of his own material old and new.

“ I’ve got some new things on the boil, and I’m really enjoying exploring my back catalogue. There’s a surprising amount of songs after forty odd years!.”

For the uninitiated, a Darren Watson show is big on dynamics, foot stomping blues grooves, and emotional pin-drop moments. There’s politics aplenty, and an awful lot of self-deprecating humour.

Watson is well-known as a powerful guitarist but what many people only realise once they hear him live is he can really sing.

Doors open 7pm for a 7.30pm start.

long_description:
For the women who have started their investment journey, dabbled in a few areas and feel pretty confident about how markets work, and are now ready for the next step - with a little support.

This workshop is your opportunity to get in a room with a Financial Adviser and review your portfolio in real time.

Elizabeth is highly qualified and experienced, but maybe more importantly, she is relatable.

As a chronic over-thinker, only child and high achiever she knows how easy it is to move too fast and commit to a range of solutions (e.g. investments) and after the fact second-guess whether they were the correct options!

If you have more than 2 investments, whether they are KiwiSaver, another Super scheme, Sharesies, Property, Term Deposits, Index Funds or Managed Funds (yes there is a difference!) then there is a good chance you are no longer able to see what your overall portfolio looks like, the risk level you are taking across the board, and whether these investments are actually getting you to where you want to be.

This workshop is limited to a very small number of women because we will be:

Discussing risk profile and money personality

Bringing in some Financial Planning concepts

Looking at some more complex concepts around building a portfolio

Looking at your personal portfolio in detail and how it aligns (or not!) with where you want to be

This workshop is ideal for anyone who has started their investing journey with enthusiasm and confidence but is now realising they've got a range of investments to manage and need clarity on how to move forward. Investments should be a tool to get to the financial future you want, let's make sure they are doing their job!

You bring your investment info, I'll bring the expertise and with some lovely women and delicious refreshments we will take a hard look at whether you are on track for where you want to go!

There will be some pre and post workshop comms and questions to ensure you get maximum value from this event.

The advantage of having an actual adviser run this event? For those that are genuinely ready to start building wealth after the workshop, there is the opportunity to work with Elizabeth 1:1 and put together a personalised Financial Plan.

Check out www.yourworth.co.nz for more details about Elizabeth and Know Your Worth.

long_description:
Well Ahead: Put your health on the agenda

An event for women balancing demanding careers, businesses and families, who are already invested in their health and want to understand it more deeply.

As energy, sleep, recovery and body composition shift through midlife, the right information matters.

Well Ahead brings together Dame Susan Devoy and a lineup of experts across health, nutrition, movement and healthy ageing to explore the science and strategy behind:

Energy and recovery

Sleep and stress

Nutrition

Strength and movement

Body composition

Hormonal changes

Perimenopause and menopause

Bone health

Genetics and individual biology

Well Ahead is designed as a connected conversation, not a series of standalone talks.

Each speaker builds on the last, giving you a clearer, more complete picture of your own health rather than a list of disconnected tips.

The day opens with an optional workshop, Your Genes, Your Choices, exploring genetics, DNA testing and the role our genes can play in understanding individual biology. The full programme continues into the afternoon and closes with a live panel and audience Q&A.

Practical information. Expert perspectives. One day, properly invested in your health.

Choose a Morning Workshop pass, Main Event pass, or the Full Pass for the whole day.




Click here to find out more.



“Women spend so much of their lives looking after everyone and everything else. Well Ahead is about putting your own health on the agenda, hearing from people who really know their field, and coming away with information and ideas you can actually use. You don't have to have all the answers. Sometimes you just need to make the time to start asking the right questions.”

- Dame Susan Devoy

long_description:
04butchclub presents SAPPHIC SESSION - a night showcasing some local sapphic and FLINTA* talent of Te Whanganui-a-Tara.

Why We're Here

Live music hits differently when you're surrounded by your community so it's about time this happens for Te Whanganui-a-Tara sapphic/FLINTA* scene. In this dedicated FLINTA* space, you will be serenaded by incredibly talented musicians and artists based in Te Whanganui-a-Tara.

As a bonus reason to party, this space was created to honour International Lesbian Day - a global celebration with deep local roots believed to have kicked off right here in Te Whanganui-a-Tara back in the 1980s!

Introducing: The Mad Butches (2026 'Make a Band' Project)

To shake things up and get talent back on stage, 04butchclub launched a 'make a band' project. In true community spirit, we gathered a group of keen singers and musicians - who haven't performed in a hot minute and had never met each other before - straight into a practice room. They've decided to be known as The Mad Butches, and maybe there's a good reason for it? Come witness the raw, collaborative magic of their very first live set!

What to expect on the night:

Open mic karaoke in the first 30min, or grab the guitar and sing a song as everyone filters in and settles into the scene.

An epic lineup - please see below for artists involved.

A couple of pool tables.

A chill, seated area for when you need to take a breather.

A table where you can enrol to vote, if you haven't already.

Timeline:

7.00pm - Doors open and open mic - choose your poison: karaoke or with guitar

7.30pm - Slam poetry from Lo

7.50pm - Comet

8.20pm - Danica Bryant

9.05pm - Mad Butches

10.05pm - Gift Horse

11.00pm - Event finish

Accessibility inside the venue:

Single-level access throughout the main venue except for the VIP area, which is up a flight of stairs.

Flashing lights (from stage and photographers) and loud sounds will be present.

Free foam earplugs will be available all night.

Important:

This is a no TERFs, no SWERFs space, and consent is mandatory. Visible event kaitiaki will be present and moving throughout the venue to help ensure everyone feels safe, respected, and supported. There will be campus security outside of the venue.

This event has been organised and will be run by volunteers. Ticket sales go towards covering the venue, equipment and paying the artists. Any profit made will go towards the following Sapphic Session 🔥👀

long_description:
Note: This is an in-person only event at Victoria University of Wellington 139 Vivian Street, Te Aro Campus

About this event:

Many challenges faced by modern society require extensive partnerships and collaboration of organisations, teams and individuals from multiple disciplines and sectors. Building skills for working across sectors is not a luxury – it is a necessity.

In this talk, Dr Sandra Mandic will introduce a framework for planning and managing cross-sector collaborations outlined in her recently published book “Compass Guide: Secrets of Successful Cross-Sector Collaborations”. She will focus on discussing project and programme management aspects of the framework, sharing her insights from initiating and leading the BEATS Research Programme in 2013-2023 – a world-class example of a successful cross-sector collaboration.

Attendees will have opportunity to reflect on their own experiences with cross-sectoral work and share their insights.

About the Presenter:

Dr Sandra Mandic, PhD, PMP is a transformational leader, innovator and award-winning researcher and author. Sandra’s personal and professional journey spans nine cities across five countries and three continents – including Europe, Canada, United States and New Zealand. She speaks four languages and has experience of working in academia, government and business. Sandra is the founder and the director of the research consultancy AGILE Research Ltd. and the creator of the Compass Guide Research Training resources (six Compass Guide books and over dozen courses) which link research and project management. She is recipient of the New Zealand Academic Achievement in Project Management Award (finalist in 2024 and winner in 2025) from PMINZ for two of her books.

Sandra is also a Research Associate at Auckland University of Technology, Team Leader Transport Strategy at Wellington City Council and was the founder and principal investigator on the award-winning BEATS Research Programme (2013-2023).

venue: 3 Market Lane, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
This workshop will demonstrate the very basics of Tukutuku where each participant will come away with a form of Tukutuku and knowledge to inspire their own mahi toi. 

All materials supplied. Prior to the workshop participants are encouraged to research Tukutuku patterns and become familiar with the meanings.

 

Artist biography.
Elena Rei
Ngāti Toarangatira, Ngāruahine, Ngāti Koata, Ngāti Tama, Sāmoa 

Elena Rei’s creative practice sits within the realm of Te Whare Pora, weaving together customary and contemporary processes of raranga, whatu muka and tukutuku. Interlaced throughout her works are collective dreams, moments of remembering and profound experiences with the materials she uses. Much of Elena’s practice is intuitive, emulating the ways of her tūpuna and drawing from a visual language that has been woven through time. Her works reimage and make familiar our inherent connection to ngā atua wāhine, through themes of aroha, grief, whakapapa and reconnection. 

Elena studied design and textiles at Massey University, where she gained early insights into practices within Te Whare Pora. A formative experience during this time was learning tukutuku under the guidance of Kohai Grace during classes at Whitireia, an experience that continues to inform her practice today.

It was the original superhighway, connecting Indigenous navigators, traders and innovators across the Pacific.
Led by ancestral wisdom and cutting-edge digital capability, the summit brings together Māori and global Indigenous tech communities to navigate the future of artificial intelligence, data sovereignty, enterprise and workforce development.

id: Chapel Of Sound II-31 Avon Street, Island Bay, Wellington 6023, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Chapel Of Sound II
venue: 31 Avon Street, Island Bay, Wellington 6023, New Zealand
long_description:
Erskine Chapel in Island Bay is considered one of the finest examples of French-Gothic architecture in NZ. Built in 1929 and restored in the 1990s, it features an Italian marble interior, soaring, vaulted ceilings and world-renown acoustics. For the first time since Erskine was built, it reeled with the sound of the underground on July 25th this year. The full audiovisual experience was a night to remember, the energy was felt by everyone there, the dancefloor was packed from start to finish, it looked and sounded incredible. So we are doing the only thing we could do; we are making it happen all over again.

As before; expect projection mapped elements, lighting to knock you sideways, sound that soars, a fully licensed bar, a decked-out chill area, a dancefloor under the arches and a collection of some of Aotearoa’s favourite selectors who will have the chapel rocking.

Dylan C is a household name. His music journey began back in the day working at Cuba Street’s Real Groovy, before moving north and embarking on a seven-year residency at Tāmaki Makaurau’s fabled Rakinos.From there, Dylan became a cornerstone of the local scene, spending 10 years as Program Director at Base FM and 15 years running the Jungle Stage at Northern Bass. He’s played almost every event you can think of, from Electric Avenue and Tora Bombora to legendary late-night and closing sets at Splore.He’s also been the vibe controller behind Shipwrecked’s Hidden Reef Stage and remains a staple across the board on any lineup. His deep, clever cuts never fail to move a dancefloor - he’s a master of his craft.

Heylady was born in Wellington in the boiler room of Tatou in the 90s. She started promoting in the early 2000s, and by 2010 had picked up the DJ bug and was playing regularly alongside internationals and locals. A well recognised name in Aotearoa’s underground, she has played the length and breadth of the country, across Australia and America. She’s one of the founding members of Taniwha’s Den, she’s one half of COMMUNICATE and co-owner of XCOMMUNICATE records. With decades of collecting killer house and techno under her belt, her well-honed ear always makes for a stomping dancefloor.

Hape has been holding it down in Wellington since the late 90s. He’s had residencies at some of the city’s most recognised establishments, brought musicians together under multiple event brands and been one of the people who have kept the scene alive. His custom brand of rolling, soul-driven sound is instantly discernible, he has a current residency at Havana Bar, and is a regular at Taniwha’s Den, his closing set last time went down in the history books.

Nam Chucks is a DJ, selector and longtime radio host at Radioactive FM. She possesses a deep respect and appreciation for sound system philosophy, dedicating her musical selections to the concepts of unity and inclusion in rave culture. She is a believer in guiding the dance and has huge respect for all things sacred and indigenous. She has played for a huge variety of events in her time, and she always holds it down.

Lady Lazerlight knocked it out of the park with her projection mapping and light show last time, so we’ve brought her back for this round.

With all this and more, we recommend arriving early. The goodness starts when the doors open and we’d hate for you to miss any of the show. Tickets are extremely limited, we suggest grabbing yours before they are gone as last time they sold out in less than 48 hours.

IMPORTANT INFO: Our event is a safe space for all. If you or someone you know is feeling unsafe or harassed, please approach one of the bar staff or security. If you are behaving badly and impacting other’s ability to have a good time you will be removed. Please act with respect and care for your fellow attendees at all times, no means no and this goes for conversations as well as more intimate requests.

Full length trailer, photos and reviews, press kit

Ange and The Boss tells the improbable story of all-time great Hungarian footballer Ferenc Puskás finding himself in Melbourne in the late 80s, coaching the Greek NSL team South Melbourne Hellas.

Barely able to speak English and comedically overweight, he united and inspired the team to a dramatic championship win in 1991. Eating, drinking, and enjoying himself along the way.

It’s a sports documentary, but it’s also a film about life in Australia. It’s about immigrant identity and belonging, gluttonous pasta consumption, and the broken window winder in Ange Postecoglou’s Datsun 200B.

long_description:
The trustees of Blue Dragon Children's Trust NZ warmly invite you to our annual fundraising film. The film we have chosen is KLARA AND THE SUN. Directed by Taika Waititi, the story is based on Kazuo Ishiguro’s accalimed novel.

What it's about:

It follows Klara, an Artificial Friend - chosen by a young girl named Josie to join her family. It's a thoughtful and emotional story exploring love, loneliness, hope and what it means to be human in our AI-driven world. The themes of AI ethics and human relationships make it great viewing for families with teenagers (M rating).

All the money we raise goes to Blue Dragon Children's Foundation in Hanoi, which works to break the poverty cycle for Vietnam's poorest children, including street kids, children with disabilities, and victims of human trafficking and slavery.

Tickets:

$25 a ticket or $30 a ticket, which includes a raffle ticket. As always, there will be at least two raffles with delicious home-made Christmas cakes and other goodies. Please bring plenty of cash on the night to buy extra raffle tickets and increase your chances of being a lucky winner.

id: Being a Good Treasurer - Hamilton Central-To be announced-Humanitix
name: Being a Good Treasurer - Hamilton Central
venue: To be announced
long_description:
A free, practical session for current and future volunteer treasurers - and for small community groups who want to feel more confident looking after their money.

Whether you’re already the treasurer, thinking about taking on the role, supporting someone else who does it, or helping run a small charity, club, society, or community group, this session is designed to make the money side feel clearer and more manageable.

We’ll talk about what makes a treasurer role work well, why the role is often harder than it should be, and simple habits that can make things easier for both the treasurer and the wider committee.

You’ll leave with a simple checklist and one practical next step for your group.

No accounting background needed. Come with your questions.

Here's what others have said after attending Being a Good Treasurer:

This was a really helpful free webinar to attend. Really clear breakdown of the treasurer role and reporting - the report template will be really useful.

I loved the concept of financial reporting being about telling your organisation's money story, this is a really great way of simplifying the concept and making it less scary.

I really liked the opportunity to see what other questions people in other NFPs had regarding this role, I also really liked the checklists and systematic way that we went through the role, it was an excellent resource thank you.

I think it's a hugely valuable workshop and I have shared it with others who might find it useful.

Big thanks to Rainbow Hub Waikato for offering their venue!

She started promoting in the early 2000s, and by 2010 had picked up the DJ bug and was playing regularly alongside internationals and locals. A well recognised name in Aotearoa’s underground, she has played the length and breadth of the country, across Australia and America. She’s one of the founding members of Taniwha’s Den, she’s one half of COMMUNICATE and co-owner of XCOMMUNICATE records. With decades of collecting killer house and techno under her belt, her well-honed ear always makes for a stomping dancefloor.

Hape has been holding it down in Wellington since the late 90s. He’s had residencies at some of the city’s most recognised establishments, brought musicians together under multiple event brands and been one of the people who have kept the scene alive. His custom brand of rolling, soul-driven sound is instantly discernible, he has a current residency at Havana Bar, and is a regular at Taniwha’s Den, his closing set last time went down in the history books.

Nam Chucks is a DJ, selector and longtime radio host at Radioactive FM. She possesses a deep respect and appreciation for sound system philosophy, dedicating her musical selections to the concepts of unity and inclusion in rave culture. She is a believer in guiding the dance and has huge respect for all things sacred and indigenous. She has played for a huge variety of events in her time, and she always holds it down.

If you are behaving badly and impacting other’s ability to have a good time you will be removed. Please act with respect and care for your fellow attendees at all times, no means no and this goes for conversations as well as more intimate requests.

id: The Trajectory of the Indian Economy over the Past Four Decades: A Story of Mixed Experiences-16 Kelburn Parade, Kelburn, Wellington 6012, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: The Trajectory of the Indian Economy over the Past Four Decades: A Story of Mixed Experiences
venue: 16 Kelburn Parade, Kelburn, Wellington 6012, New Zealand
long_description: The lecture will discuss India’s developmental experience over the past four decades. Since this is a vast subject, the discussion will be limited to only some of the principal features. India’s experience is one of mixed messages, both positive and negative. India historically recorded a low growth rate, around 3.5%. This was accompanied by a high tariff regime along with bureaucratic controls that have been described as a ‘license permit raj’. India experienced a serious balance of payments crisis in 1991 with foreign reserves barely enough to pay for 2 weeks’ food imports. This set in motion a series of trade liberalisation reforms initiated by the then Finance Minister, Dr Manmohan Singh, consisting of removal of trade barriers and reduction of high tariffs on several items. This propelled India to one of the fastest growing economies accompanied by increase in per capita income and reduction in poverty. India ranks third on aggregate GDP (on PPP) though on per capita GDP she falls well down the list. India’s sizeable middle-class swamps that of the EU and many of the smaller economies thus providing a large market. There has been widespread digitalisation of transactions leading to reduction in corruption. But there has also been a large increase in inequality and according to the World Inequality report, 2026, India is one of the most unequal countries in the world. There is lack of skilled jobs to employ the educated youth making India unable to exploit the advantage of ‘demographic dividend’ she enjoys over China. The talk will compare living standards between India and China.

id: The Lady’s Not for Burning-106 Cashmere Avenue, Khandallah, Wellington 6035, New Zealand  ·  Accessibility info-Humanitix
name: The Lady’s Not for Burning
venue: 106 Cashmere Avenue, Khandallah, Wellington 6035, New Zealand  ·  Accessibility info
long_description:
The Lady's Not for Burning will entrance you with its sparkling humour, witty wordplay, poetic lyricism, satisfying love stories and occasional excoriations of the follies of humankind.

Will world-weary discharged soldier Thomas Mendip achieve his desire for death by hanging?

Who will sweet young convent-raised Alizon Eliot marry - the stuffy older brother or the impetuous younger one? Or neither?

Will the Mayor and the Justice of the small market-town of Cool Clary really give in to the mob and burn as a witch the vivacious and spirited Jennet Jourdemayne in the morning?

The Lady's Not for Burning, set in "1400, either more or less or exactly", is one of Christofer Fry's most well-known works. First performed in 1948, its life-affirming post-war optimism was an instant success with audiences and critics alike. Today, its humour and delightful storytelling are just as enjoyably satisfying as they were then.

This is a community theatre production by special arrangement with Concord Theatricals and The Play Bureau.

id: NZ Photographers of Cultural Collections Forum 2026-55 Cable Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: NZ Photographers of Cultural Collections Forum 2026
venue: 55 Cable Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
NZ Photographers of Cultural Collections is a group of photographers and imaging professionals working across Galleries, Libraries, Archives, and Museums across Aotearoa. We photograph cultural collections from paintings through to scientific specimens, and from intangible culture, through flat copy digitisation to 3D scanning. 

The forum is a chance to share knowledge and build professional networks. It provides valuable professional development that is otherwise hard to come by for this specialised field. We specifically aim to help smaller institutions by democratising specialist knowledge and building a network of support across the country. This year we have hybrid capability, and welcome physical event (paid) online-only (free) registrations.

This event relies on volunteers and institutional support. Thanks to Te Papa Tongarewa for donating the venue and kaimahi time, and National Services Te Paerangi for funding and administrative support and additional travel support for eligible attendees. Kaimahi from NZ maritime Museum, Auckland University of Technology, Auckland City Libraries, Puke Ariki and Archives NZ/National Library have collaborated to organise the event this year.

These contributions help keep costs down, the physical registration fee will help to cover a venue set up fee and a catered morning tea and lunch for in-person attendees.

Online attendees will receive an email with the zoom link closer to the date.

We intend to record the event via zoom. If we decide to distribute recordings in any form, we will seek the permission of speakers before doing so.

We'll be closing registrations for in-person attendees at 4pm Friday 6th Nov.

We have an online network here: https://groups.io/g/NZPCC
For any pātai please email us at: nzpcccommittee@gmail.com

Mum's & Bub's — A 4-Week Connection Series

Join us for a relaxed, expert-led series designed to support you through those early postpartum months - no pressure, no judgement, just a space to connect.

Each week we welcome a different guest expert to share their knowledge and answer your questions on the topics that matter most after having a baby. While you listen, chat and ask away, bub has their own comfy little play space set up right there in the room - so there's no need to juggle or step away.

Sessions are split by age group, so you're with mums at a similar stage

Each day there are three session time options - 10.15am, 11.30am

🚼 Thursdays
Starting Thursday 8th October, running for 4 weeks

Week 1 — Thursday 8th October: Lactation/Feeding/Pumping with Jo from BlissfulBubs

Week 2 — Thursday 15th October: Starting Solids with Dr Julie from Dr Julie Bhosale

Week 3 — Thursday 22nd October: Naturopathic postpartum care with Anna from Anna Reeves Naturopathy

Week 4 — Thursday 29th October: Sleep with Fran from thegentlesleepconsultant

Each session is limited to 10 mums to keep the space calm and supportive. When selecting the ticket - this will be the time group you're in each week, and the ticket price covers all 4 weeks.

What's Included

A new guest expert each week, covering key postpartum topics

Open Q&A - bring your questions, nothing is off-limits

A comfy, safe play space for bub within the session

Light morning tea provided

Time to connect with other local mums going through the same stage

☕ BYO coffee welcome (with lid to keep babies safe)

Pricing

$120 for the full 4 weeks (Girl maths $30 per session)

Pricing is per Mum - so twin/multiple mums only need the 1 ticket

What to Know

Feeding, crying and leaving early are all completely okay

We'll come together as a group at the start to introduce ourselves - no pressure to be on time, the doors will stay open, and the expert talk is expected to begin around 20 minutes in

These sessions are suited for first-time or multiple-time mums. Tickets are per mum (twin mums just need the one ticket)

venue: 22 Tennyson Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Restoring what was wounded. 

Recovering what was lost. 

Becoming who God created us to be.

 

Do you at times struggle to fully embrace your identity as a son or daughter of God? Do you feel like you know who you are in Christ, but struggle to walk in it completely?

Then this event is for you!

 

Join us for a powerful journey of healing, hope, restoration, and discovery of your identity in Christ led by Sandra Sellmer-Kersten.

Through biblical teaching, prayer ministry, and compassionate support, you’ll be invited to encounter Jesus in the places where you’ve experienced pain and discover His invitation to healing and wholeness.

Whether you are personally seeking healing or want to gain some tools to help others walk in and embrace their identity in Christ, this event offers practical insights, spiritual encouragement, and opportunities for prayer and ministry.

 

Sessions include:

The Heart: Restoring what has been wounded and broken.

The Identity: Remembering who God says we are—and learning to live from that truth.

The Voice: Recovering what shame, fear, pain, and rejection have silenced.

The Song: Reawakening the unique “song” God has sung over each of us from the beginning.

The Calling: Rediscovering what we were created for—and stepping into what God has entrusted to us with His power and authority. 

 

What to Expect:

Biblical teaching on trauma and healing

Opportunities to receive prayer

A safe, compassionate, and supportive environment

Encouragement, hope, and practical tools for restoration

Included in your ticket:

Morning and afternoon tea will be provided, but please bring your own lunch

A comprehensive manual, usually sold separately for $25

About Sandra:
Sandra Sellmer-Kersten is the founder of House of Nacham Ministries, New Zealand, which she leads alongside her husband, Peter. She previously served for nine years with Elijah House Ministries USA, where she worked as a prayer minister and teacher under the leadership of John and Paula Sandford. Since moving to New Zealand, Sandra began working alongside Elijah House New Zealand, where she facilitates schools, teaches lessons, and has served as a Small Group Leader for 14 years.

Sandra has a deep passion for seeing people encounter the healing love and transforming power of Jesus Christ. Through teaching, prayer ministry, mentoring, and training, she helps people understand the impact of trauma and woundedness, and to find healing, rediscover their God-given identity, and step more fully into who God created them to be.

Her teaching combines biblical truth, practical understanding, personal experience, and more than two decades of ministry experience, with an emphasis on creating a safe and compassionate space for people to honour their stories and encounter Jesus.

This event is not suitable for those under 16.

id: Global ChangeLabs: Breakfast w/ Banny Banerjee & co (WLG)-30 Waring Taylor Street, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Global ChangeLabs: Breakfast w/ Banny Banerjee & co (WLG)
venue: 30 Waring Taylor Street, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Designing Desirable Transformations in a Complex World

With Banny Banerjee and a panel of Aotearoa changemakers.

The challenges we face today; from technological disruption and climate change to organisational transformation and societal change... are increasingly complex, interconnected and difficult to solve through any single intervention.

So how do we design transformations in the context of complex, systemic, and interconnected challenges?

Join us for a special conversation with Banny Banerjee, founder of Global ChangeLabs and Adjunct Professor at Stanford University’s Doerr School of Sustainability.

Before launching Global ChangeLabs, Banny founded Stanford ChangeLabs and spent two decades working across fields and exploring how to approach complex and deeply integrated challenges and design genuinely transformative pathways. Earlier in his career, Banny worked at IDEO during the period when the firm was helping pioneer what became known as Design Thinking.

For this special event, Banny will share insights about how conventional wisdom and deterministic approaches are increasingly ill suited to address the deeply systemic and integrated nature of our challenges.  He will share how his work across sectors - business, government, technology, sustainability and social systems indicates the need for new capacities, leadership models, organizational functions, and platforms to address an uncertain and increasingly complex future.  Given his work on how to leverage a diversity of perspectives, we will also be joined by a panel of local change-makers to explore what these ideas might mean in the Aotearoa New Zealand context.

We’ll explore:

How do we embrace the complexity rather than expect isolated solutions to work?

How must we reframe design and innovation to shape interventions that shift the trajectory of a system?

How do we effectively combine different disciplines, perspectives and ways of thinking?

How do we identify opportunities for meaningful intervention and make them actionable?

What new forms of leadership, collaboration and organisational architecture might be needed for systemic transformation?

How might Aotearoa NZ become a place to demonstrate transformative ways of approaching complex challenges.  What can Aotearoa NZ contribute and learn... Especially, as we navigate our own economic, technological, environmental and societal transitions?

This will be an opportunity to hear a distinctive international perspective, connect it with the experiences of people working on complex challenges here in Aotearoa, and consider what it might mean to design the conditions for a different future.

Who is this for?

Anyone working to create meaningful change in complex environments: including leaders, designers, strategists, innovators, entrepreneurs, policymakers, researchers, funders, social-sector practitioners and people working across organisational and sector boundaries.

Come curious.

Bring a complex challenge.

Leave with new perspectives on where, and how, change might be possible.

We'd love for you to join us for this breakfast event, to explore how we can Designing Desirable Transformations in a Complex World

id: Power Up Central Hutt-6 Myrtle Street, Hutt Central, Lower Hutt 5040, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Power Up Central Hutt
venue: 6 Myrtle Street, Hutt Central, Lower Hutt 5040, New Zealand
long_description:
Power Up the Hutt – Central Lower Hutt

A more comfortable home. Lower energy bills. Greater peace of mind.

If you've been wondering whether electrification could make a real difference to your home and your household budget, this free community event is the perfect place to start.

Join us at Hutt Bowling Club, 6 bMyrtle Street on Thursday 29 October at 7:30 pm for an informative and welcoming evening where local people share how they've transformed the way they live.

From warmer homes in winter and lower running costs to cleaner indoor air and greater energy independence, electrification is helping Hutt Valley households enjoy a better quality of life while reducing their environmental impact.

You'll hear firsthand experiences from local residents who have installed heat pumps, solar panels, home batteries, electric hot water systems, induction cooktops and electric vehicles. They'll explain what motivated them, what the process was like, what they would do differently, and the benefits they're now enjoying every day.

Whether you're just beginning to explore your options or you're ready to take the next step, you'll leave with practical ideas, greater confidence, and a clearer understanding of where to begin.

This is a community event—not a sales presentation. There are no technical lectures or pressure to buy anything. Just honest conversations, practical advice, and the opportunity to ask questions in a relaxed and friendly setting.

Businesses, schools and community organisations interested in electrification are also welcome.

Free admission. Everyone welcome.

Come along and discover how simple changes today can create a home that's more comfortable, more affordable to run, and better prepared for the future.

long_description:
Hailing from the music-filled streets of Melbourne, Australia, Shaun Kirk is an award-winning blues and soul troubadour recognised for his exceptional talent as a born entertainer. His unique talent has not only earned him many accolades but also much praise from fellow artists, such as three-time Grammy Award Winner Fantastic Negrito, who has declared his show as "One of the best one-man shows he’s ever seen!"

Kirk's vocals exude a gritty, soulful depth that seems to transcend far beyond his years, with critics continually acclaiming him as "one of the finest blues voices Australia has ever heard" (Buzz Mag). Complementing his vocal artistry, Kirk's vintage guitar tones and raw grooves pay tribute to the timeless influences that have shaped his musical journey, resulting in a distinctive sound fast becoming his own.

Shaun’s musical journey has taken him to stages all over the world, where he's not only performed but consistently sold out shows, leaving audiences enthralled by his magnetic presence. From iconic festival stages like Bluesfest Byron Bay, where he's become a familiar name, to sharing the billing with legends like Robert Plant of Led Zeppelin, John Mayer, Paolo Nutini, John Butler Trio, and The Teskey Brothers; Kirk's artistic prowess is in esteemed company. Moreover, he's also had the honour of opening for household names such as blues maestro Joe Bonamassa, soul sensation Allen Stone, and the indomitable Beth Hart; further solidifying his place in the landscape of contemporary music. This remarkable journey is a testament to Kirk's unmatched talent and ability to connect with audiences across genres and generations.

WHAT THE PRESS IS SAYING ABOUT SHAUN KIRK

“It’s rare to see someone bring down the house as an opener, but Australia’s Shaun Kirk did exactly that. He connected with the crowd immediately” – Soundcheck Entertainment, Canada

“One of the most explosive acts Australia has to offer” – Mixdown Magazine, Australia

"My faith in this generation’s music has been restored.” - Dearhead Press

“Simply astounding." - Forte Magazine, Australia
